cau_hoi: According to the legend "The Dragon and the Fairy", the ancestors of the Vietnamese are Lạc Long Quân and who?
giai_thich: The story tells that Lạc Long Quân, of the Dragon lineage, married the fairy Âu Cơ. Âu Cơ gave birth to a pouch of a hundred eggs, which hatched into a hundred children. Later, 50 children followed their father to the sea, and 50 followed their mother to the mountains. The eldest son was honored as king, known as Hùng Vương. Therefore, the Vietnamese proudly call each other "brothers and sisters" (from the same pouch).

cau_hoi: Who defeated the Southern Han army on the Bạch Đằng River in 938, opening a long period of independence for the country?
giai_thich: Ngô Quyền had his troops drive wooden stakes with sharp iron tips into the bed of the Bạch Đằng River. When the tide rose, he lured the enemy ships in; when the tide receded, the enemy ships got stuck on the stakes and were defeated. The victory in 938 ended over 1,000 years of Northern domination. Later, the Trần dynasty also used the same tactic of driving stakes in the Bạch Đằng River to defeat the Mongol army.

cau_hoi: In the year 40, which two sisters led the uprising against the Eastern Han's oppression?
A: Ỷ Lan and Dương Vân Nga
B: The Two Trưng Sisters (Trưng Trắc and Trưng Nhị)
D: Bùi Thị Xuân and Võ Thị Sáu
giai_thich: The Two Trưng Sisters were daughters of the Lạc general of Mê Linh. Trưng Trắc's husband, Thi Sách, was killed by the governor Tô Định. The two sisters raised the flag of rebellion and quickly captured 65 citadels. Trưng Trắc became queen, establishing her capital in Mê Linh. The Two Sisters symbolize the patriotism and indomitable spirit of Vietnamese women.

cau_hoi: Who read the Declaration of Independence that established the Democratic Republic of Vietnam on September 2, 1945?
giai_thich: In Ba Đình Square, Hanoi, before about half a million people, President Hồ Chí Minh read the Declaration of Independence. The declaration begins by quoting the American Declaration of Independence (1776) and the French Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen (1789). September 2 became Vietnam's National Day.

cau_hoi: Thăng Long is the old name of which city today?
giai_thich: In 1010, King Lý Thái Tổ moved the capital from Hoa Lư to Đại La and renamed it Thăng Long, meaning "ascending dragon", because according to legend, he saw a golden dragon flying up as his boat docked. Thăng Long was the capital of many dynasties. In 1831, King Minh Mạng renamed it Hà Nội, meaning "the city inside the river".

cau_hoi: According to legend, which boy from Phù Đổng village grew into a warrior, riding an iron horse to fight the Ân invaders?
giai_thich: Gióng, at three years old, still could not speak or smile. When he heard the messenger looking for someone to fight the invaders, he suddenly asked to go, then grew rapidly. Gióng rode an iron horse, wielded an iron rod to defeat the enemy; when the rod broke, he uprooted bamboo to strike the invaders. Afterward, Gióng flew back to heaven on Sóc Mountain. The Gióng Festival at Phù Đổng Temple and Sóc Temple is an intangible cultural heritage of humanity.

cau_hoi: What was the name of the first state in the history of Vietnam?
giai_thich: The Văn Lang state, led by the Hùng kings, was formed around the 7th century BC, in the Red River Delta, the Mã River, and the Cả River regions. The capital was located in Phong Châu (Phú Thọ). The Văn Lang people cultivated wet rice, cast bronze, and practiced the custom of dyeing their teeth and chewing betel. Later, Văn Lang was succeeded by the Âu Lạc state of An Dương Vương.

cau_hoi: According to legend, who made the bánh chưng and bánh giầy to present to King Hùng?
giai_thich: King Hùng wanted to choose a successor, so he asked his children to find delicious offerings to present to their ancestors. Lang Liêu, the poorest, was advised by a deity to use glutinous rice to make cakes: bánh chưng, square-shaped, symbolizes the earth, and bánh giầy, round-shaped, symbolizes the sky. The king was very pleased and passed the throne to Lang Liêu. Since then, bánh chưng has become an indispensable dish during the Lunar New Year.

cau_hoi: In the legend "Sơn Tinh, Thủy Tinh", which two deities competed to marry whom?
A: Mỵ Châu, daughter of An Dương Vương
C: Mỵ Nương, daughter of King Hùng
giai_thich: King Hùng the 18th was choosing a husband for his daughter Mỵ Nương. Sơn Tinh arrived first with the wedding gifts and married Mỵ Nương. Thủy Tinh, angry, raised the water to fight Sơn Tinh, but the higher the water rose, the higher the mountains became. The legend explains the phenomenon of annual floods and reflects the ancient Vietnamese people's will to combat natural disasters.

cau_hoi: On which lunar date is the Hùng Vương Commemoration Day celebrated?
giai_thich: The folk saying "No matter who goes back and forth, remember the Hùng King's Commemoration Day on the tenth of the third month" reminds everyone to remember their roots. The largest festival takes place at Hùng Temple, Phú Thọ. Since 2007, this day has become an official holiday. In 2012, UNESCO recognized "The Worship of Hùng Kings in Phú Thọ" as an intangible cultural heritage of humanity.

cau_hoi: Which famous citadel did An Dương Vương order to be built, shaped like a spiral?
giai_thich: Co Loa Citadel (now in Dong Anh district, Hanoi) was built around the 3rd century BC, consisting of many earthen ramparts with a water moat surrounding it. Legend has it that the citadel kept collapsing until the Golden Turtle God helped complete its construction. This is the oldest and largest citadel that still remains in Vietnam.

cau_hoi: In which year did the famous victory of Dien Bien Phu, "a triumph that shook the world," occur?
giai_thich: On May 7, 1954, the Vietnamese army led by General Vo Nguyen Giap defeated the French stronghold of Dien Bien Phu. This victory forced France to sign the Geneva Accords, ending the war in Indochina. It was the first time a colonized nation defeated a colonial power in a major campaign, inspiring liberation movements worldwide.

cau_hoi: In which year did King Ly Thai To move the capital to Dai La and rename it Thang Long?
giai_thich: In the spring of 1010, Ly Cong Uan issued the "Edict on Moving the Capital," explaining that Hoa Lu was cramped, while Dai La was centrally located, spacious, and flat, facilitating transportation. In 2010, Hanoi celebrated the 1,000th anniversary of Thang Long – Hanoi. The year 1009 marks the establishment of the Ly dynasty.

cau_hoi: Which invading army did Tran Hung Dao lead the Tran people against?
giai_thich: The Tran dynasty defeated the Mongol – Yuan army three times (1258, 1285, and 1287 – 1288), an army that had conquered from China to Europe. Tran Hung Dao was the commander-in-chief during the two later resistance wars. He is revered by the people as "Saint Tran" and is worshipped in many places. He is one of the most outstanding generals in world history.

cau_hoi: Where did Le Loi raise the flag to start the uprising against the Ming army?
giai_thich: In 1418, Le Loi, a wealthy leader in Lam Son, declared himself the King of Binh Dinh and launched the uprising. In the early years, the insurgents faced many difficulties, sometimes having to eat wild vegetables and tubers. After 10 years, the uprising succeeded, and Le Loi ascended to the throne in 1428, establishing the Early Le dynasty.

cau_hoi: According to the legend of Hoan Kiem Lake, to whom did King Le Loi return the sacred sword?
giai_thich: The legend states that Le Loi was lent a divine sword by the Dragon King to fight against the Ming invaders. When peace was restored, the king was boating on Hoan Kiem Lake when the Golden Turtle emerged to reclaim the sword. Since then, the lake has been called Hoan Kiem Lake (Sword Lake), meaning "lake of the returned sword." The Turtle Tower in the middle of the lake was built in the late 19th century.

cau_hoi: Who is the author of "Truyen Kieu," a masterpiece of Vietnamese literature?
giai_thich: Nguyen Du (1765 – 1820) wrote "Doan Truong Tan Thanh," commonly known as Truyen Kieu, consisting of 3,254 verses in the traditional Vietnamese six-eight meter. The work narrates the tumultuous life of Thuy Kieu. Truyen Kieu has been translated into dozens of languages, and many verses have become proverbs. In 2015, UNESCO honored Nguyen Du on the 250th anniversary of his birth.

cau_hoi: What date marks the liberation of the South and the reunification of the country?
giai_thich: On the afternoon of April 30, 1975, tanks of the Liberation Army entered the Independence Palace in Saigon, ending the approximately 21-year-long resistance against the Americans. The final campaign was named the Ho Chi Minh Campaign. In 1976, Saigon was renamed Ho Chi Minh City. April 30 and May 1 are major public holidays in Vietnam.

cau_hoi: The Temple of Literature in Hanoi, built in 1070, is dedicated to whom?
giai_thich: In 1070, King Ly Thanh Tong ordered the construction of the Temple of Literature to honor Confucius and the sages of Confucianism, while also serving as a school for the crown prince. The Temple of Literature – Quoc Tu Giam is considered the first university in Vietnam. Today, many students come here to pray for luck before exams.

cau_hoi: The famous bronze drums of the ancient Vietnamese belong to which culture?
giai_thich: The Dong Son culture developed about 2,500 years ago and is named after Dong Son village (Thanh Hoa), where the first artifacts were discovered in 1924. The Dong Son bronze drum features a star shape in the center, surrounded by images of the Lạc bird, rice pounders, stilt houses, and racing boats. The bronze drum is a symbol of the Red River civilization.

cau_hoi: What is the real name of King Quang Trung?
giai_thich: Nguyễn Huệ was the second brother among the three Tây Sơn brothers. He was a military genius, undefeated in major battles. In 1788, he ascended to the throne, taking the reign name Quang Trung, and marched north to defeat the Qing army. He died in 1792 at the age of 39, leaving many reform plans unfinished.

cau_hoi: Which invading army was defeated by King Quang Trung in the great spring victory of the Year of the Rooster (1789)?
giai_thich: The Qing army, consisting of about 290,000 troops, invaded Thăng Long at the request of Lê Chiêu Thống. King Quang Trung marched rapidly from Phú Xuân to the north, allowing his troops to celebrate Tet early, and then attacked right during Tet. In just 5 days, the Qing army was defeated at Ngọc Hồi and Đống Đa. Every year, Hanoi holds the Đống Đa festival on the 5th day of Tet.

cau_hoi: What was the last feudal dynasty of Vietnam?
giai_thich: The Nguyễn Dynasty was established by Emperor Gia Long in 1802 and lasted until 1945 with 13 emperors. From 1884, the Nguyễn Dynasty was under French protection. The last emperor was Bảo Đại, who abdicated in August 1945. The Nguyễn Dynasty left many architectural works in Huế, which are now a World Heritage Site.

cau_hoi: In which city was the capital of the Nguyễn Dynasty located?
giai_thich: Emperor Gia Long chose Phú Xuân (Huế), a land that the Nguyễn lords had built for a long time, as the capital. The citadel of Huế was constructed starting in 1805, featuring a system of walls, palaces, and monumental tombs along the Perfume River. In 1993, the Complex of Monuments of the Imperial City of Huế became the first World Heritage Site recognized by UNESCO in Vietnam.

cau_hoi: In 248, Lady Triệu (Triệu Thị Trinh) led a rebellion against which occupying army?
giai_thich: Lady Triệu was from Thanh Hóa and is famous for her saying: "I want to ride the strong winds, tread the fierce waves, slay the giant fish in the East Sea, drive out the Wu army, reclaim the homeland, and break the chains of slavery, rather than bow down to be a concubine for anyone!" She wore golden armor and rode an elephant into battle. The rebellion failed, and she sacrificed herself at the age of 23.

cau_hoi: In 544, Lý Bí ascended to the throne and named the country what?
giai_thich: After defeating the Liang army, Lý Bí proclaimed himself Lý Nam Đế and named the country Vạn Xuân, hoping for the nation to endure through countless springs. He was the first Vietnamese to claim the title "Emperor," on par with the northern emperors. He ordered the construction of Khai Quốc Pagoda, the precursor to Trấn Quốc Pagoda in present-day Hanoi.

cau_hoi: What local warlord conflict did Đinh Bộ Lĩnh end to unify the country in 968?
giai_thich: After Ngô Quyền's death, the Ngô dynasty weakened, and local leaders divided the land among themselves, known as the "12 Warlord Rebellion." Đinh Bộ Lĩnh, from Hoa Lư, gradually defeated them and was honored by the people as "Vạn Thắng Vương." In 968, he ascended to the throne as Đinh Tiên Hoàng, ending over 20 years of turmoil.

cau_hoi: Where was the capital of the Đinh and Early Lê dynasties located?
giai_thich: Hoa Lư is a rugged limestone mountain area in Ninh Bình, the homeland of Đinh Bộ Lĩnh, making it easy to defend. The capital is surrounded by mountain ranges like a natural wall. Today, there are still temples dedicated to King Đinh and King Lê in Hoa Lư. The Tràng An scenic complex, which includes the ancient capital of Hoa Lư, is a mixed cultural and natural World Heritage Site.

cau_hoi: What national title did Đinh Tiên Hoàng give to our country?
giai_thich: "Đại Cồ Việt" means "Great Vietnam," reflecting the spirit of independence and self-reliance. This national title was used from 968 to 1054, when Emperor Lý Thánh Tông changed it to Đại Việt. King Đinh also established the reign title Thái Bình and minted the Thái Bình Hưng Bảo coins, the first coins of our country.

cau_hoi: In 1911, the young man Nguyễn Tất Thành (later known as President Hồ Chí Minh) left to seek a way to save the country from which port?
giai_thich: On June 5, 1911, Nguyễn Tất Thành, then 21 years old, took the name Văn Ba and applied to be a cook on the French merchant ship Amiral Latouche-Tréville, leaving from Nhà Rồng Wharf. He traveled through many countries in Europe, Africa, and America, taking various jobs to make a living. He returned to his homeland after 30 years, in 1941. The Nhà Rồng building by the port is now the Hồ Chí Minh Museum.

cau_hoi: In which battle did the poem "Nam quốc sơn hà" resonate during the fight against the Song army?
B: Battle of the Như Nguyệt River
D: Battle of Ngọc Hồi – Đống Đa
giai_thich: In 1077, when the Song army attacked the Như Nguyệt River defenses, according to legend, the poem "The mountains and rivers of Nam, the king of Nam resides, clearly defined by heaven's decree..." echoed in the night. The poem uplifted our troops. It is often referred to as the first declaration of independence of Vietnam, and is associated with the name Lý Thường Kiệt.

cau_hoi: Who is the author of "Bình Ngô đại cáo", considered the second declaration of independence of Vietnam?
giai_thich: In 1428, after driving out the Ming army, Nguyễn Trãi wrote "Bình Ngô đại cáo" on behalf of King Lê Lợi to announce to the world. The famous opening line is "The essence of humanity and righteousness lies in the peace of the people." The work affirms that Đại Việt has a long-standing cultural heritage, with its own territory, customs, and history. Nguyễn Trãi was a great military leader, politician, and poet.

cau_hoi: Which group did King Trần Thánh Tông summon to the Diên Hồng Conference in 1284 to seek opinions on whether to negotiate or fight against the Mongol army?
giai_thich: Faced with the threat of a second Mongol invasion, the retired Emperor Trần Thánh Tông invited elders representing the entire nation to the Diên Hồng Palace to seek their opinions. They all shouted in unison, "Fight!" The conference demonstrated the spirit of national unity and is considered a form of early democracy in Vietnamese history.

cau_hoi: Which young man from the Trần dynasty crushed an orange in frustration for not being allowed to participate in state affairs, then went home to recruit troops under the banner "Defeat the strong enemy, repay the royal grace"?
giai_thich: In 1282, when the king was discussing the plan to fight the Mongol army, 15-16 year old Trần Quốc Toản was not allowed to attend due to his age. In frustration, he crushed the orange given by the king. Later, Trần Quốc Toản returned home to gather over a thousand followers, made a red flag embroidered with six golden characters, and fought bravely in the resistance. This story was recounted by writer Nguyễn Huy Tưởng in "The Flag Embroidered with Six Golden Characters."

cau_hoi: Which dynasty built the One Pillar Pagoda (Diên Hựu Tự) in Hanoi?
giai_thich: In 1049, King Lý Thái Tông dreamt of the Bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara sitting on a lotus throne leading him to a platform. Following the advice of a monk, the king ordered the construction of a pagoda on a stone pillar in the middle of a lake, resembling a lotus rising from the water's surface. The pagoda was destroyed in 1954 and rebuilt in 1955. It is one of the symbols of Hanoi.

cau_hoi: According to the Geneva Agreement in 1954, at which latitude was Vietnam temporarily divided?
giai_thich: The Geneva Agreement stipulated that latitude 17, along the Bến Hải River (Quảng Trị), would serve as a temporary military demarcation line, with national unification elections scheduled after two years. However, the elections did not take place, and the country was divided for about 21 years. The Hiền Lương Bridge over the Bến Hải River is a symbol of this division. Latitude 38 is the demarcation line in the Korean Peninsula.

cau_hoi: Which French missionary made significant contributions to the development of the Vietnamese national language based on the Latin alphabet?
giai_thich: The Vietnamese national language is the result of the efforts of many Western missionaries (Portuguese, Italian, French) along with Vietnamese collaborators in the 17th century. Alexandre de Rhodes systematized and published the Vietnamese-Portuguese-Latin dictionary in 1651. Initially, the national language was used for missionary work, and it only became widely adopted in the early 20th century, becoming the official writing system.

cau_hoi: When was the first examination held to select talented individuals for government positions in our country?
giai_thich: In 1075, King Lý Nhân Tông opened the examination "Minh kinh bác học và Nho học tam trường". The top candidate in this examination was Lê Văn Thịnh, who later became the Grand Tutor. From then on, the examination system in Vietnam lasted over 800 years, until the last examination in 1919 during the reign of King Khải Định.

cau_hoi: When was Quốc Tử Giám, the first university in our country, established?
giai_thich: In 1076, King Lý Nhân Tông established Quốc Tử Giám next to Văn Miếu, initially to educate the children of the royal family and nobility. Later, during the Trần and Lê dynasties, the school expanded to accept talented children from common families. The famous teacher Chu Văn An once held the position of Deputy Principal of Quốc Tử Giám during the Trần dynasty.

cau_hoi: In which year did King Lý Thánh Tông change the name of the country from Đại Cồ Việt to Đại Việt?
giai_thich: The name Đại Việt was used for the longest time in Vietnamese history, through the Lý, Trần, Lê, Mạc, and Tây Sơn dynasties, with only a brief interruption during the Hồ dynasty (Đại Ngu). It was not until 1804 that King Gia Long changed the name to Việt Nam. King Lý Thánh Tông was also the one who ordered the construction of Văn Miếu in 1070.

cau_hoi: In the Battle of Rạch Gầm – Xoài Mút on the Tiền River, which invading army did Nguyễn Huệ defeat?
giai_thich: In 1785, Nguyễn Ánh sought help from Siam (Thailand), and about 50,000 Siamese troops invaded Gia Định. Nguyễn Huệ set up an ambush along the Tiền River from Rạch Gầm to Xoài Mút (now Tiền Giang), luring the enemy into the battlefield and then defeating them. Only a few thousand Siamese soldiers survived and fled back home. This was one of the largest naval battles in the history of Vietnam.

cau_hoi: When was the Communist Party of Vietnam established?
giai_thich: The conference to unify communist organizations, chaired by Nguyễn Ái Quốc, took place in Cửu Long (Hong Kong, China) in early 1930. February 3 was chosen as the founding date of the Party. May 19, 1941, is the founding date of the Việt Minh Front, which coincides with the birthday of President Hồ Chí Minh (May 19, 1890).

cau_hoi: In the Battle of Bạch Đằng in 938, which natural phenomenon did Ngô Quyền exploit to defeat the Southern Han army?
giai_thich: The Bạch Đằng River near the estuary is strongly influenced by the tide. Ngô Quyền had stakes driven in during low tide, and when the tide rose, the stakes were hidden. He sent light boats to challenge the enemy and pretended to retreat. When the tide receded, the enemy's large ships got stuck on the stakes and sank. This tactic was later used by the Trần dynasty in 1288.

cau_hoi: Who was the commander of the Southern Han army killed in the Battle of Bạch Đằng in 938?
giai_thich: Hoằng Tháo was the son of the Southern Han king Lưu Cung. The Southern Han king sent his son to invade our country while he himself stayed at the border waiting for reinforcements. Upon hearing that his son had been killed and the army was defeated, the Southern Han king "grieved and wept, gathering the remaining soldiers to retreat." Liễu Thăng was a Ming general, and Ô Mã Nhi was a Yuan general.

cau_hoi: In 939, where did Ngô Quyền declare himself king and establish his capital?
giai_thich: Ngô Quyền chose Cổ Loa, the ancient capital of An Dương Vương, to affirm the continuity of the nation's founding tradition from the Âu Lạc period. He abolished the title of military governor from the Northern feudal lords, established civil and military positions, and regulated court ceremonies. The Ngô dynasty marked the beginning of a long period of independence and self-reliance for the nation.

cau_hoi: In 980, who ascended the throne and founded the Early Lê dynasty?
giai_thich: When King Đinh Tiên Hoàng and his eldest son were assassinated, the new king Đinh Toàn was only 6 years old, while the Song army was preparing to invade. General Lê Hoàn was elevated to king by the generals and the Empress Dowager, becoming Lê Đại Hành. He defeated the Song army in 981 and conquered Champa. Note that the Lê dynasty of Lê Lợi is referred to as the Later Lê (Lê sơ).

cau_hoi: Which Empress Dowager presented the dragon robe to Lê Hoàn, inviting him to become king to lead the resistance against the Song?
giai_thich: Dương Vân Nga was the wife of King Đinh Tiên Hoàng and the mother of the young king Đinh Toàn. In the face of the threat of foreign invasion, she prioritized the country's interests over her family's, presenting the dragon robe to Lê Hoàn. She later became the queen of Lê Đại Hành, thus being called the "queen of two dynasties." Her temple is located in Hoa Lư, Ninh Bình.

cau_hoi: In which year did Lê Hoàn lead the army and people to defeat the Song invasion?
giai_thich: In 981, the Song army divided into two routes, by land and by water, to invade our country. Lê Hoàn commanded the forces to block them at the Bạch Đằng River and on land at Chi Lăng, killing the enemy general Hầu Nhân Bảo and forcing the Song army to retreat. This victory helped consolidate independence and forced the Song to recognize Lê Hoàn. The year 1077 was when the Lý dynasty defeated the Song army for the second time.

cau_hoi: Legend has it that in his childhood, Đinh Bộ Lĩnh, while herding buffaloes, often used what as a flag to play war games with his friends?
giai_thich: Đinh Bộ Lĩnh lost his father at a young age and lived with his mother in Hoa Lư. While herding buffaloes, he was often honored by his friends as a "general," sitting cross-legged as a palanquin bearer and using reed flowers as flags to practice military tactics. The story of "reed flags in military practice" shows his leadership skills from a young age. Later, he quelled the rebellion of the 12 warlords and ascended to the throne.

cau_hoi: In 1075, Lý Thường Kiệt proactively led his troops to attack the Song territory to destroy the base preparing for invasion, including which city?
giai_thich: Lý Thường Kiệt advocated that "waiting for the enemy to come is not as good as taking the initiative to strike first to block the enemy's spearhead." Our troops attacked the bases of Khâm Châu, Liêm Châu, and besieged Ung Châu (now Nanning) for more than 40 days before capturing the city, destroying the enemy's granaries and arsenals. He then withdrew to prepare defensive lines against the Song army.

cau_hoi: Which river did Ly Thuong Kiet build the Như Nguyệt defense line on to block the Song army in 1077?
giai_thich: Như Nguyệt River is a section of the Cau River flowing through Bac Ninh, blocking the route from the border to Thang Long. Ly Thuong Kiet ordered the construction of thick dikes and multi-layered bamboo fences along the southern bank. The Song army could not cross and suffered heavy losses. Ultimately, Ly Thuong Kiet proactively suggested a truce for the Song army to retreat, maintaining long-term peace.

cau_hoi: Which king did Queen Yi Lan help govern the country while he went to fight the Champa?
giai_thich: Yi Lan came from a girl who picked mulberries in Tho Loi village (Gia Lam). In 1069, when Ly Thanh Tong went to fight Champa, she stayed in the capital to manage state affairs, ensuring the people's stability. Later, she helped her son, King Ly Nhan Tong, who was still young, to govern the country. She is considered an outstanding female politician in history.

cau_hoi: Who was the last king of the Ly dynasty and also the only queen in Vietnamese history?
giai_thich: Ly Chieu Hoang (real name Ly Phat Kim) ascended the throne in 1224 at about 6 years old. Just over a year later, under the arrangement of Tran Thu Do, she abdicated in favor of her husband Tran Canh, ending the Ly dynasty after 216 years. Trung Trac also once declared herself queen, but Ly Chieu Hoang is the only empress of the feudal regime in Vietnam.

cau_hoi: In 1225, to whom did Ly Chieu Hoang abdicate, opening the Tran dynasty?
giai_thich: Tran Canh, about 8 years old, was the nephew of Tran Thu Do, brought into the palace to be a companion to Ly Chieu Hoang. Tran Thu Do arranged for the two to marry, and then Chieu Hoang abdicated in favor of her husband. Tran Canh became the first king of the Tran dynasty, known as Tran Thai Tong. The Tran dynasty lasted for 175 years.

cau_hoi: Who played a decisive role in transferring the throne from the Ly to the Tran dynasty and held real power in the early years of the Tran dynasty?
giai_thich: Tran Thu Do was the uncle of King Tran Thai Tong, holding the title of Grand Master. He was a strict and fair person, not favoring relatives. Once, when his wife asked for a position for a relative, he made that person cut off a toe to distinguish them from others, causing that person to be frightened and withdraw. He played a significant role in establishing a strong Tran dynasty.

cau_hoi: The saying "My head has not yet fallen to the ground, please do not worry, Your Majesty" during the Mongol invasion in 1258 was said by whom?
giai_thich: When the Mongol army invaded, King Tran Thai Tong anxiously asked for advice from the officials. Grand Marshal Tran Nhat Hao advised to temporarily retreat to Song. The king sought out Tran Thu Do, who boldly replied with the above statement, showing determination to fight the enemy. This statement boosted the morale of the king and the court.

cau_hoi: Which famous work of Tran Hung Dao called on the generals to study military strategy and be determined to fight the enemy?
giai_thich: "Hich Tuong Si" was written before the second resistance war against the Yuan. Tran Hung Dao criticized the playfulness and indulgence of the generals and expressed his feelings: "I often forget to eat at mealtime, and at midnight I beat my knee... even if my hundred bodies are exposed on the grass, and my thousand corpses are wrapped in horse skin, I would be happy." This hich is an immortal patriotic political essay.

cau_hoi: In the Battle of Bach Dang in 1288, which commander of the Yuan navy was captured by the Tran army?
giai_thich: In 1288, Tran Hung Dao ordered stakes to be placed on the Bach Dang River, similar to the method used by Ngo Quyen in 938. When O Ma Nhi's fleet retreated along the river, our troops lured the enemy into the stake field at low tide and then attacked. The entire fleet was destroyed, and O Ma Nhi was captured. This was the greatest victory that ended the third resistance war.

cau_hoi: Which Yuan prince had to hide in a copper pipe to escape back home after the defeat in 1285?
giai_thich: Thoat Hoan was the son of Ho Tat Liet, commanding the Yuan army invading our country for the second and third times. In 1285, when the Yuan forces were in retreat, to avoid the arrows of our troops, Thoat Hoan had to hide in a copper pipe carried by his soldiers. Upon returning home, he was angrily exiled by Ho Tat Liet to Yangzhou, never to meet again.

cau_hoi: Who was the Tran general famous for the story of being so absorbed in state affairs that he did not notice when a soldier stabbed him in the thigh?
giai_thich: Pham Ngu Lao was sitting weaving baskets by the roadside, so absorbed in thinking about military strategy that when Tran Hung Dao's army passed by, the soldiers shouted to clear the way without him noticing, and he was stabbed in the thigh but did not move. When Tran Hung Dao inquired, he saw his talent and brought him back to serve and married his adopted daughter to him. He became a famous general and the author of the poem "Thuật Hoài."

cau_hoi: Which king of the Trần dynasty, after defeating the Mongol army, became a monk and founded the Trúc Lâm Zen sect?
giai_thich: Trần Nhân Tông was a king during the two resistance wars against the Mongols in 1285 and 1288. In 1293, he abdicated in favor of his son, and in 1299 he retreated to Mount Yên Tử to practice Buddhism, founding the Trúc Lâm Zen sect, a school of Zen that embodies Vietnamese identity. He is revered as the 'Buddha King'. The Trúc Lâm sect emphasizes the spirit of engagement, linking the path with life.

cau_hoi: What is the center of the Trúc Lâm Zen sect of Vietnamese Buddhism located on which mountain?
giai_thich: Yên Tử Mountain (Quảng Ninh) is approximately 1,068 meters high and is known as the 'cradle' of Trúc Lâm Buddhism. The mountain features a system of pagodas, hermitages, and towers, with Đồng Pagoda located at the highest peak. Every year, the Yên Tử festival attracts millions of pilgrims. In 2025, the Yên Tử – Vĩnh Nghiêm – Côn Sơn, Kiếp Bạc complex was recognized by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

cau_hoi: In 1306, Princess Huyền Trân was married to King Chế Mân of Champa. In return, Đại Việt received which territory?
A: Ba châu Địa Lý, Ma Linh, Bố Chính
giai_thich: Huyền Trân was the daughter of King Trần Nhân Tông. King Chế Mân offered the two regions of Ô and Lý (now southern Quảng Trị, Thừa Thiên Huế, and part of Quảng Nam) as a bridal gift. The two regions were renamed Thuận Châu and Hóa Châu, later known as Thuận Hóa. Less than a year later, Chế Mân died, and Huyền Trân was brought back to her homeland by General Trần Khắc Chung.

cau_hoi: Which famous teacher during the Trần dynasty submitted the 'Thất trảm sớ' asking for the execution of seven sycophants?
giai_thich: Chu Văn An was one of the most respected teachers, serving as the Principal of the Quốc Tử Giám, teaching the crown prince. During the reign of King Trần Dụ Tông, when the court was in decline, he submitted a petition to execute seven sycophants, but the king did not heed his advice. He then resigned and retreated to Chí Linh, where he taught and wrote books. He is worshipped at the Văn Miếu alongside Confucius.

cau_hoi: In 1400, Hồ Quý Ly ascended the throne and changed the name of our country to what?
giai_thich: Hồ Quý Ly was a powerful minister at the end of the Trần dynasty. In 1400, he deposed the Trần king and ascended the throne, establishing the Hồ dynasty and changing the country's name to Đại Ngu, meaning 'great joy' (the term 'Ngu' here means joy, not ignorance). He implemented many bold reforms in the economy, education, and military. The Hồ dynasty lasted only 7 years before being invaded by the Ming army.

cau_hoi: The Hồ Dynasty Citadel (Tây Đô Citadel), built with gigantic stone blocks, is located in which province?
giai_thich: The citadel was constructed by Hồ Quý Ly in 1397 in just about 3 months. The walls were assembled using large green stones, some weighing over 20 tons, without the need for mortar, and they still stand strong today. In 2011, the Hồ Dynasty Citadel was recognized by UNESCO as a World Cultural Heritage Site. This is the only stone citadel of its kind remaining in Southeast Asia.

cau_hoi: The Hồ Dynasty issued the first paper money in our country, what was it called?
giai_thich: In 1396, while still serving in the Trần dynasty, Hồ Quý Ly ordered the printing of paper money 'Thông bảo hội sao', with denominations featuring images of dragons, waves, clouds, turtles, unicorns, and phoenixes. He forced the people to exchange their copper coins for paper money, and anyone caught counterfeiting was executed. However, the populace was not accustomed to using paper money, so the reform faced difficulties. To date, no paper money from this period has been found.

cau_hoi: Which general of the Lam Sơn insurgents disguised himself as Lê Lợi, risking his life to break through the enemy encirclement to save his commander?
giai_thich: In 1419, the insurgents were tightly besieged by the Ming army at Chí Linh Mountain. Lê Lai volunteered to wear a robe, ride an elephant, and claim to be Lê Lợi to charge out and distract the enemy. The Ming troops thought they had killed their commander and retreated, allowing Lê Lợi to escape danger. Remembering this act of bravery, later King Lê Lợi instructed his descendants to honor Lê Lai's death anniversary a day before his own. There is a saying in folklore: 'On the 21st Lê Lai, on the 22nd Lê Lợi.'

cau_hoi: In the Battle of Chi Lăng in 1427, which general of the Ming army was beheaded by the Lam Sơn insurgents?
giai_thich: In 1427, the Ming dynasty sent Liễu Thăng to lead 100,000 troops to assist. When passing through Chi Lăng Pass (Lạng Sơn), in the treacherous terrain, Liễu Thăng was ambushed and killed. After that, our troops continued to defeat this army at Xương Giang. The troops of Mộc Thạnh, upon hearing the news, also panicked and fled. This victory forced Vương Thông in Đông Quan to surrender.

cau_hoi: What is the most progressive and complete legal code of the feudal period in Vietnam, issued during the reign of King Lê Thánh Tông, called?
A: Hồng Đức Code (Quốc triều hình luật)
giai_thich: The Hồng Đức Code (named after the Hồng Đức era of Lê Thánh Tông) consists of about 722 articles. The code has many progressive points, such as protecting the rights of women: daughters inherit like sons, and wives have the right to own property. The code also includes provisions to protect the elderly, children, and the disabled.

cau_hoi: Which king led the famous Tao Dan poetry club in the 15th century?
giai_thich: Le Thanh Tong (reigned 1460 – 1497) was a king skilled in literature, who self-identified as the leader of Tao Dan. The club consisted of 28 literary officials, likened to the 28 stars in the sky (Nhi thap bat tu). The time of Le Thanh Tong is considered one of the most prosperous periods of the feudal system in Vietnam, with many achievements in law, education, and culture.

cau_hoi: Nguyen Binh Khiem, a famous poet and prophet of the 16th century, is commonly known by what name among the people?
giai_thich: Nguyen Binh Khiem passed the top scholar exam in 1535 during the Mac dynasty and was granted the title Trinh Tuyen Hầu, hence the name Trang Trinh. He is famous for his prophetic verses, and many times the Mac, Trinh, and Nguyen forces sought his counsel. Trang Luong refers to Luong The Vinh, while Trang Quynh is a humorous folk character.

cau_hoi: Which river served as the boundary dividing the South (Nguyen Lords) and the North (Trinh Lords) during the 17th – 18th centuries?
giai_thich: The Gianh River flows through Quang Binh province. From 1627 to 1672, the two feudal factions of Trinh and Nguyen fought seven times without a victor, ultimately using the Gianh River as the boundary, dividing the country for about 150 years. The Ben Hai River (17th parallel) became the dividing line after 1954.

cau_hoi: The Cau Pagoda, a symbol of Hoi An ancient town, is believed to have been built by merchants from which country in the early 17th century?
giai_thich: In the 16th – 17th centuries, Hoi An was a bustling trading port where Japanese and Chinese merchants established trading quarters. The Cau Pagoda (also known as the Japanese Bridge) connects the Japanese quarter with the Chinese quarter. In 1719, Lord Nguyen Phuc Chu named it "Lai Vien Kieu" (bridge welcoming distant guests). The image of Cau Pagoda is printed on the 20,000 dong banknote.

cau_hoi: In 1788, Nguyen Hue ascended to the throne as Emperor, taking the reign name Quang Trung, where?
giai_thich: Upon hearing that the Qing army had occupied Thang Long, Nguyen Hue established a ceremony to worship heaven and earth at Ban Mountain, south of Phu Xuan, and ascended to the throne on December 22, 1788, to legitimize his leadership against the invaders. Shortly after, he personally led his troops northward. Today, there is a worship site and a statue of Emperor Quang Trung on Ban Mountain in Hue.

cau_hoi: In the battle of Ngoc Hoi – Dong Da in 1789, which Qing general committed suicide by hanging himself at Dong Da hill?
giai_thich: Sam Nghi Dong was the governor of Dien Chau, commanding the Khương Thượng post (Dong Da). When the post was attacked by the Tay Son army, he despaired and hanged himself. Ton Si Nghi was the overall commander of the Qing army, fleeing across the floating bridge over the Red River in panic, to the extent that he did not have time to put on his armor. Today, Dong Da hill has a statue of Emperor Quang Trung.

cau_hoi: Who was the commander of the Qing army that fled in panic when the Tay Son forces entered Thang Long in 1789?
giai_thich: Ton Si Nghi was the governor of Liangguang, commanding about 290,000 troops sent to our country under the pretext of assisting Le Chieu Thong. After occupying Thang Long, the Qing forces became complacent, focusing on celebrating Tet. When they heard that the Tay Son army was advancing, Ton Si Nghi panicked, "the horse was not saddled, and the person did not have time to wear armor," and hurriedly fled across the floating bridge. The bridge broke, causing many Qing soldiers to drown.

cau_hoi: On what date according to the lunar calendar did Emperor Quang Trung decisively defeat the Qing army and enter Thang Long?
C: The 5th of Tet in the Year of the Rooster
D: New Year's Eve of the Year of the Rooster
giai_thich: Emperor Quang Trung ordered his troops to celebrate Tet early on the 30th of the last month and promised to enter Thang Long to celebrate on the 7th of Tet. In reality, at noon on the 5th of Tet in the Year of the Rooster (January 30, 1789), the emperor entered the city, two days earlier than planned. According to legend, the emperor's battle robe was blackened by gunpowder smoke. The Dong Da Hill Festival is held annually on the 5th of Tet.

cau_hoi: Which famous female general of the Tay Son dynasty was tasked with commanding the elephant troops?
giai_thich: Bui Thi Xuan was from Binh Dinh, skilled in martial arts, and was the wife of General Tran Quang Dieu. She was appointed as Admiral, commanding the elephant troops and participating in many major battles. When the Tay Son dynasty collapsed, she was captured by Nguyen Anh and executed brutally, but she remained defiant and unafraid. Many schools are named after her.

cau_hoi: Who are the three brothers of the Tay Son dynasty, including Nguyen Nhac, Nguyen Hue, and who?
giai_thich: The three brothers originally had the surname Ho, later changed to their mother's surname Nguyen. In 1771, they raised the flag of rebellion in Tay Son village. Nguyen Nhac was the eldest, proclaiming himself Emperor Thai Duc; Nguyen Lu was granted the title Dong Dinh Vuong, guarding the South; while Nguyen Hue was a military genius. Note that the Tay Son dynasty had no familial ties with the Nguyen lords or the Nguyen dynasty.

cau_hoi: Which province is the homeland of the Tay Son movement today?
giai_thich: Tay Son village is located in the western region of Binh Dinh. Here lies the Quang Trung Museum, which houses an ancient tamarind tree and a well believed to belong to the three brothers. Binh Dinh is also known as the "land of martial arts" famous for the traditional Tay Son martial arts and the Tay Son battle drum. According to the administrative arrangement in 2025, Binh Dinh province will be merged into Gia Lai province.

cau_hoi: During the reign of King Quang Trung, which script was promoted and used in official documents?
giai_thich: King Quang Trung wanted to elevate the national language, so he issued the "Edict on Establishing Schools" and required the use of Nom script in edicts and examinations. He established the Sung Chinh Institute led by La Son Phu Tu Nguyen Thiep to translate books from Han script to Nom script. Nom script is a writing system created by the Vietnamese based on Han script to transcribe the Vietnamese language.

cau_hoi: In what year did Nguyen Anh ascend to the throne as emperor, taking the reign name Gia Long and founding the Nguyen dynasty?
giai_thich: After defeating the Tay Son dynasty, Nguyen Anh ascended the throne in 1802 in Phu Xuan, taking the reign name Gia Long, which signifies the connection from Gia Dinh (Saigon) to Thang Long. For the first time in over 200 years, the country was unified from North to South with a territory nearly as large as today. In 1804, he established the national name Vietnam.

cau_hoi: In what year was the national name "Vietnam" officially used for the first time?
giai_thich: In 1804, King Gia Long established the national name as Vietnam. Initially, he wanted to use the name "Nam Viet", but the Qing dynasty disagreed because it was similar to the ancient name of Nam Viet from Trieu Da, so it was changed to "Vietnam". During Minh Mang's reign, the national name was changed to Dai Nam. Since 1945, the name Vietnam has been used again and continues to this day.

cau_hoi: Which king of the Nguyen dynasty changed the national name from Vietnam to Dai Nam?
giai_thich: Minh Mang (reigned 1820 – 1841) was a king who implemented many important administrative reforms, dividing the country into provinces, most of which are still used today. He changed the national name to Dai Nam, meaning "great land of the South". He also had the Nine Urns cast and placed in the The Mieu (Hue), on which images of the country's mountains, rivers, and products were engraved.

cau_hoi: During the time of the Nguyen lords and the Nguyen dynasty, what was the purpose of the "Hoang Sa Team"?
A: To go to the Paracel Islands to exploit resources and assert sovereignty
C: To protect the royal palace in Hue
giai_thich: From the 17th century, the Nguyen lords established the Hoang Sa Team consisting of about 70 men, mainly from An Vinh village (Ly Son Island, Quang Ngai). Each year they would go to the islands for about 6 months, collecting seafood, goods from shipwrecks, surveying, and marking the territory. In Ly Son, there is an annual ceremony called the Khao Le Thế Lính Hoàng Sa to commemorate the soldiers who have gone.

cau_hoi: In 1858, where did the French colonists first open fire to begin their invasion of Vietnam?
giai_thich: On September 1, 1858, the French and Spanish coalition attacked the Son Tra peninsula (Da Nang). They intended to strike quickly and then advance to Hue. However, the Da Nang troops under the command of Nguyen Tri Phuong implemented a "no empty garden" strategy, causing the French forces to be bogged down for many months, with many soldiers dying from illness. In 1859, the French shifted their focus to attack Gia Dinh.

cau_hoi: In 1861, which French warship did Nguyen Trung Truc lead his troops to burn on the Nhat Tao River?
giai_thich: On December 10, 1861, Nguyen Trung Truc and his troops disguised themselves as wedding guests, approached, and burned the French ship Espérance on the Nhat Tao River (Long An). This was a resounding victory, praised by poet Nguyen Dinh Chieu as "Fire of Nhat Tao shaking the heavens and earth". He later captured the Kien Giang fort.

cau_hoi: The famous saying "When will the Westerners remove all the grass of Nam, then the people of Nam will stop fighting the West" is attributed to whom?
giai_thich: In 1868, the French captured Nguyen Trung Truc's mother to threaten him, forcing him to surrender. Before being executed in Rach Gia, he uttered the famous words above, expressing his indomitable spirit. He sacrificed himself at the age of about 30. His temple is located in Rach Gia, and many places in Kien Giang bear his name.

cau_hoi: What title was given to Truong Dinh, the leader of the anti-French resistance in Go Cong, by the people?
giai_thich: In 1862, when the Hue court signed a treaty ceding three provinces in southeastern Vietnam to the French and ordered Truong Dinh to disband his troops, he refused to comply and stayed to fight alongside the people. The people honored him as "Binh Tay Grand Marshal" (Grand Marshal against the Western invaders). In 1864, betrayed and besieged, he committed suicide to avoid falling into enemy hands.

cau_hoi: In 1862, which treaty did the Hue court sign to cede three provinces in Eastern South Vietnam to France?
giai_thich: The Nhâm Tuất Treaty (June 5, 1862) forced the court to cede the three provinces of Bien Hoa, Gia Dinh, and Dinh Tuong, as well as Con Lon Island, to France, opening the seas for French trade and compensating for war expenses. The treaty caused public outrage. In 1867, France continued to occupy three provinces in the West (Vinh Long, An Giang, Ha Tien) without needing to fight.

cau_hoi: Which treaty signed in 1884 officially established France's long-term protectorate over all of Vietnam?
giai_thich: The Patenôtre Treaty (June 6, 1884), named after the French representative Jules Patenôtre, divided Vietnam into Nam Ky (colony), Trung Ky (managed by the Hue court in name only), and Bac Ky (protectorate). The seal of the Qing dynasty given to King Nguyen was melted down in front of both parties. The treaty marked Vietnam's official transition to a semi-feudal colonial state.

cau_hoi: In 1885, in the name of which king did Ton That Thuyet issue the "Royal Edict for the King", calling on scholars and the people to rise up to save the country?
giai_thich: After the failed counterattack against French forces in the imperial city of Hue (July 1885), Ton That Thuyet took the 14-year-old King Hàm Nghi to Tan So (Quang Tri) and issued the Royal Edict for the King. "Cần Vương" means "help the king". The movement spread throughout Northern and Central Vietnam for over 10 years. In 1888, King Hàm Nghi was captured and exiled to Algeria.

cau_hoi: Who led the Hương Khê uprising (1885 – 1896), the largest uprising of the Cần Vương movement?
giai_thich: Phan Đình Phùng passed the highest doctoral examination and once served as an imperial censor. He led the insurgents in the mountainous region of Ha Tinh, along with General Cao Thắng, who manufactured rifles based on French models. When the French exhumed ancestors' graves and captured relatives to force surrender, he remained resolute. He died in 1895 due to illness, and the uprising ended in 1896.

cau_hoi: Who was the leader of the Yên Thế peasant uprising, known as the "Yên Thế Tiger"?
giai_thich: The Yên Thế uprising (Bắc Giang) lasted about 30 years (1884 – 1913), making it the longest peasant uprising against French colonialism. Đề Thám relied on the treacherous mountains, forcing the French to negotiate multiple times. In 1913, he was assassinated by French agents. Đề Thám did not follow the Royal Edict for the King but fought to protect the farmers' land.

cau_hoi: Which movement did Phan Bội Châu initiate to send Vietnamese youth to Japan for study?
giai_thich: After Japan defeated Russia in 1905, Phan Bội Châu believed that he could rely on Japan to learn and fight against France. The Eastern Study Movement (1905 – 1908) sent about 200 youths to Japan for education. In 1908, France colluded with Japan to expel Vietnamese students. Phan Bội Châu was arrested in 1925 and placed under house arrest in Hue until his death, earning the nickname "The Old Man of Bến Ngự."

cau_hoi: What path to national salvation did Phan Châu Trinh advocate?
A: Relying on Japan to fight against France
B: Reform, raise public awareness, and civil rights peacefully
giai_thich: Phan Châu Trinh believed in "enlightening the public, uplifting the spirit, and improving living conditions" (expanding public awareness, enhancing morale, and improving livelihoods), opposing the monarchy and advocating for democratic reforms. He opposed reliance on foreign powers. He was a pioneer of the Duy Tân movement in Central Vietnam. In 1926, his funeral in Saigon became a large public demonstration.

cau_hoi: The Đông Kinh Nghĩa Thục school, established in 1907 to provide free education and promote new ideas, was founded in which city?
giai_thich: "Đông Kinh" was the name for Hanoi at that time, and "Nghĩa Thục" means a school for the sake of justice, without charging tuition. The school was founded by Lương Văn Can, Nguyễn Quyền, and patriotic Confucians, teaching the Vietnamese language, science, history, and advocating for the abolition of superstitions. The school operated for only about 9 months before being closed by the French colonizers.

cau_hoi: In 1916, King Duy Tân participated in an uprising against the French but failed and was exiled to where?
giai_thich: King Duy Tân ascended the throne in 1907 at the age of 7. As he grew up, he secretly contacted the Vietnam Quang Phuc Association led by Thái Phiên and Trần Cao Vân. The uprising plan in May 1916 was leaked, and he was captured and exiled to Réunion Island in the Indian Ocean. He died in 1945 in a plane crash in Africa. His remains were returned to Hue in 1987.

cau_hoi: Who was the last king of the Nguyễn dynasty and also the last king of the feudal system in Vietnam?
giai_thich: Bảo Đại (Nguyễn Phúc Vĩnh Thụy) ascended the throne in 1926 while studying in France. On August 30, 1945, he abdicated, handing over the imperial seal to the representative of the provisional government at Ngọ Môn, Hue, with the famous words, "I would rather be a citizen of an independent country than a king of a subjugated nation." He died in 1997 in Paris.

cau_hoi: In 1911, Nguyễn Tất Thành left to seek a way to save the country while working as a cook on which ship?
giai_thich: Amiral Latouche-Tréville was a merchant ship of the Five Star company (Chargeurs Réunis) from France. Nguyễn Tất Thành, under the name Văn Ba, worked as a cook with very hard labor from early morning until late at night. The ship passed through Singapore, Colombo, Port Said to Marseille (France). From there, he traveled through many countries, gaining experience and seeking a way to save the country.

cau_hoi: After 30 years of working abroad, in 1941, leader Nguyễn Ái Quốc returned to the country and lived and worked at which location?
giai_thich: On January 28, 1941, Nguyễn Ái Quốc crossed the border back to the country, staying in the Cốc Bó cave in Pác Bó. He named the stream Lenin Stream and the mountain Marx Mountain. His poem "Tức cảnh Pác Bó" includes the line "In the morning by the stream, at night in the cave, porridge made from bamboo shoots is always ready." In May 1941, the 8th Central Conference took place here.

cau_hoi: In which year was the Việt Minh Front (Vietnam Independence League) established?
giai_thich: On May 19, 1941, at the 8th Central Conference in Pác Bó, the Việt Minh Front was established to unite all classes of people, regardless of class or religion, to fight the French, expel the Japanese, and gain independence. The front gathered the "National Rescue Associations" of workers, farmers, youth, and women. The Việt Minh led the successful August Revolution in 1945.

cau_hoi: On what date did the August Revolution successfully seize power in Hanoi?
giai_thich: On August 19, 1945, hundreds of thousands of people in Hanoi gathered at the Grand Theater and then advanced to seize the Governor-General's Palace, the City Hall, and the Police Department. On August 23, the revolution succeeded in Hue, and on August 25 in Saigon. In just about 15 days, the revolution succeeded nationwide. August 19 is commemorated annually as the day of the successful August Revolution.

cau_hoi: Where did President Hồ Chí Minh read the Declaration of Independence in 1945?
giai_thich: On September 2, 1945, at Ba Đình flower garden (now Ba Đình Square), President Hồ Chí Minh read the Declaration of Independence. While reading, he paused and asked, "Can my compatriots hear me clearly?", to which the entire square responded loudly. Today, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is located next to this square.

cau_hoi: "The call for nationwide resistance" against French colonialism by President Hồ Chí Minh was issued on what date?
giai_thich: On the night of December 19, 1946, the resistance war broke out in Hanoi. On the morning of December 20, the call was broadcast on the radio, with the famous line "No! We would rather sacrifice everything than lose our country, than become slaves." The military and people of Hanoi fought to defend the capital for 60 days and nights so that the leadership could safely retreat to Việt Bắc.

cau_hoi: Who was the general commanding the French stronghold of Điện Biên Phủ, captured alive on May 7, 1954?
giai_thich: De Castries was promoted to brigadier general right in the midst of the battle. On the afternoon of May 7, 1954, the soldiers of the Vietnam People's Army entered the command bunker, hoisted the flag "Determined to fight, determined to win" on the roof of the bunker, and captured him along with the entire General Staff. Navarre was the commander of French forces in Indochina, who planned the construction of Điện Biên Phủ.

cau_hoi: How many days and nights did the Điện Biên Phủ campaign in 1954 last?
giai_thich: The campaign began on March 13, 1954, and ended successfully on May 7, 1954, lasting 56 days and nights. The poet Tố Hữu wrote, "Fifty-six days and nights digging mountains, sleeping in caves, in pouring rain, eating rice balls." Hundreds of thousands of laborers carried rice and pushed bicycles loaded with goods over mountains to serve the campaign. "12 days and nights" refers to the time of the "Điện Biên Phủ in the air" battle in 1972.

cau_hoi: The Hòa Bình culture, a famous culture named after a province of Vietnam, belongs to which period?
giai_thich: The Hòa Bình culture dates back about 18,000 to 7,500 years ago. In 1932, the Congress of Prehistoric Scholars of the Far East officially named it "Hòa Bình culture" after Hòa Bình province, where French archaeologist Madeleine Colani discovered many relics. The inhabitants lived in caves, hunted, gathered, and may have begun primitive farming. This culture has also been found in many Southeast Asian countries.

cau_hoi: The Ngọc Lũ bronze drum, one of the most beautiful Đông Sơn bronze drums, was found in which province?
giai_thich: The drum was discovered in 1893 – 1894 when locals were building a dyke in Ngọc Lũ commune, Bình Lục district, Hà Nam. The drum face features a 14-pointed star in the center, surrounded by decorative bands with images of the Lạc bird, deer, stilt houses, drummers, and rice pounders. This is a national treasure, currently displayed at the National History Museum. According to the administrative arrangement in 2025, Hà Nam province will be merged into Ninh Bình province.

cau_hoi: The Sa Huỳnh culture, famous for the practice of burying the dead in ceramic jars, developed in which region of Vietnam?
giai_thich: The Sa Huỳnh culture (around 1000 BC – 200 AD) is named after the Sa Huỳnh site in Quảng Ngãi, where jar tombs were discovered in 1909. The inhabitants of Sa Huỳnh were skilled in ironworking, jewelry making with gemstones and glass, especially in crafting double-headed animal earrings. They traded by sea with many regions in Southeast Asia. This culture laid the foundation for the later Champa kingdom.

cau_hoi: The Mỹ Sơn Sanctuary in Quảng Nam, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, was the religious center of which kingdom?
giai_thich: Mỹ Sơn consists of about 70 temples and towers, built continuously from the 4th to the 13th century, mainly dedicated to the Hindu god Shiva. The towers were constructed using baked bricks, and scientists still do not fully understand the bonding techniques used. Many towers were heavily damaged by bombs during the war. In 1999, Mỹ Sơn was recognized by UNESCO as a World Heritage Site.

cau_hoi: The Óc Eo archaeological site, the commercial center of the Funan kingdom, is located in which province today?
giai_thich: Óc Eo is located in Thoại Sơn district, An Giang, at the foot of Ba Thê mountain, excavated by French archaeologist Louis Malleret in 1944. Here, Roman coins, Chinese bronze mirrors, and Indian jewelry were found, proving it was once a bustling international port on the maritime route connecting the East and the West. In 2025, the Óc Eo – Ba Thê site is being nominated as a World Heritage Site.

cau_hoi: In the legend of An Dương Vương, what did Mỵ Châu scatter on the path while fleeing to help her husband Trọng Thủy track her?
giai_thich: Mỵ Châu wore a coat made of goose feathers. Trọng Thủy instructed her to scatter goose feathers if there was turmoil so he could find her. When the army of Triệu Đà attacked, Mỵ Châu sat behind her father fleeing and scattered the feathers, causing the enemy to pursue. The turtle god Kim Quy appeared and said, 'The enemy is behind the king,' leading An Dương Vương to execute Mỵ Châu and then take a seven-inch horn down to the sea.

cau_hoi: Trọng Thủy, who deceived An Dương Vương to obtain the divine crossbow, is the son of whom?
giai_thich: Triệu Đà was the king of Nam Việt, who repeatedly attacked Âu Lạc without success due to the divine crossbow. He used a marriage proposal strategy, allowing his son Trọng Thủy to marry Mỵ Châu and live as a son-in-law. Trọng Thủy devised a way to swap the crossbow's trigger and then returned to his homeland. Triệu Đà then sent troops to attack, leading to An Dương Vương's defeat. Legend has it that Trọng Thủy later regretted his actions and committed suicide by jumping into a well in Cổ Loa.

cau_hoi: Mã Viện, the general who led the army to suppress the Hai Bà Trưng uprising in 42 – 43, was a general of which dynasty?
giai_thich: Mã Viện was an elderly general of the Eastern Han Dynasty, leading about 20,000 troops and 2,000 boats to attack. The Hai Bà Trưng fiercely resisted at Lãng Bạc and then at Cẩm Khê. In 43, the two sisters sacrificed themselves (legend has it they jumped into the Hát River). After the victory, Mã Viện is said to have erected a bronze pillar at the southern border. He is referred to by the Chinese folk as 'Phục Ba tướng quân.'

cau_hoi: After the successful uprising in 40, Trưng Trắc became queen and established her capital where?
giai_thich: Mê Linh (now part of Hanoi) is the homeland of the Hai Bà Trưng. Trưng Trắc ascended the throne, declaring herself Trưng Vương, and exempted the people from taxes for two years. The Hai Bà Trưng Temple in Mê Linh and the Đồng Nhân Temple in Hanoi are dedicated to the two sisters. Luy Lâu (Bắc Ninh) was the administrative center of the colonial government during the Northern domination and an early center of Buddhism.

cau_hoi: The famous saying 'I want to ride the strong wind, tread the fierce waves, and slay the giant fish in the East Sea...' belongs to which female hero?
giai_thich: Bà Triệu (Triệu Thị Trinh) was born in 226 in Thanh Hóa. When her brother advised her to marry, she replied with the above saying, expressing her great ambition. In 248, she, along with her brother Triệu Quốc Đạt, led a rebellion against the Ngô army. Folklore states that she was 9 feet tall and had a voice like a bell. The tomb of Bà Triệu is located in Tùng Mountain, Thanh Hóa.

cau_hoi: Triệu Quang Phục relied on which swamp to continue the resistance against the Lương army after Lý Nam Đế's defeat?
giai_thich: Đầm Dạ Trạch (Hưng Yên) is a marshy area with dense reeds. Triệu Quang Phục had his troops hide during the day and at night row bamboo boats to ambush the enemy, then retreat back to the swamp. The Lương army could not advance. In 550, he defeated the Lương army and ascended the throne, calling himself Triệu Việt Vương. He is popularly known as 'Dạ Trạch Vương.'

cau_hoi: Mai Thúc Loan, the leader of the uprising against the Tang dynasty in 713, was known by what name?
giai_thich: Mai Thúc Loan was from Nghệ An, born into a poor family and worked as a salt carrier. Once, when he had to carry fabric to pay tribute to the Tang dynasty, he called upon fellow laborers to rise up. He declared himself emperor, established his capital in Vạn An (Nghệ An), and due to his dark skin, he was popularly called 'Mai Hắc Đế' (Black Emperor of the Mai clan). The uprising attracted hundreds of thousands of participants.

cau_hoi: Phùng Hưng, the leader of the uprising against the Tang dynasty in the late 8th century, was honored by the people as what?
giai_thich: Phùng Hưng was born in Đường Lâm (Sơn Tây, Hanoi), known for his extraordinary strength, rumored to be able to wrestle down buffaloes and defeat tigers. He, along with his brother Phùng Hải, led the uprising and captured the city of Tống Bình (Hanoi). After his death, the people honored him as "Bố Cái Đại Vương", meaning the king regarded as a parent of the people. The ancient village of Đường Lâm still has a temple dedicated to him and Ngô Quyền.

cau_hoi: Khúc Thừa Dụ, who initiated the period of autonomy for our country, seized control from the Tang dynasty in what year?
giai_thich: In 905, the Tang dynasty weakened. Khúc Thừa Dụ, a local leader in Hồng Châu (Hải Dương), was supported by the people, captured the city of Đại La, and proclaimed himself as Tiết độ sứ. Although he still held the title of the Tang dynasty, he effectively gained autonomy for the country. His son, Khúc Hạo, implemented many reforms. The victory at Bạch Đằng in 938 completely ended the period of Northern domination.

cau_hoi: Dương Đình Nghệ, who expelled the Southern Han army in 931, was killed by whom to seize power?
giai_thich: In 937, the general Kiều Công Tiễn killed Dương Đình Nghệ to take the position of Tiết độ sứ. When he was attacked by Ngô Quyền, the son-in-law of Dương Đình Nghệ, Kiều Công Tiễn sought help from the Southern Han. The Southern Han king took this opportunity to invade. Ngô Quyền killed Kiều Công Tiễn first, then defeated the Southern Han army on the Bạch Đằng River in 938.

cau_hoi: What was the relationship between Ngô Quyền and Dương Đình Nghệ?
giai_thich: Ngô Quyền was from Đường Lâm, skilled in martial arts, trusted by Dương Đình Nghệ, who married his daughter Dương Thị Như Ngọc to him. He was assigned to govern the region of Ái Châu (Thanh Hóa). When his father-in-law was killed by Kiều Công Tiễn, Ngô Quyền led an army north to punish the traitor. Đường Lâm is known as "land of two kings" because it is the homeland of both Phùng Hưng and Ngô Quyền.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the first coin minted by the feudal state of Vietnam under King Đinh Tiên Hoàng?
giai_thich: The Thái Bình Hưng Bảo coin was minted around 970, during the reign of King Đinh, and is the first coin of Vietnam. The coin is made of bronze, round with a square hole in the middle for stringing. The reverse side has the character "Đinh", the name of the dynasty. The ability to mint coins reflects the sovereignty and independence of the nation.

cau_hoi: "Chiếu dời đô" of King Lý Thái Tổ was written in what script?
giai_thich: At that time, Hán script was the official writing system used in state documents, examinations, and literature. The "Chiếu dời đô" is about 214 characters long, outlining the reasons for relocating the capital and praising Đại La as "situated in the center of heaven and earth, with the shape of a dragon coiling and a tiger sitting". Nôm script became more widely used in literature from the Trần dynasty and was elevated to official status during the Tây Sơn dynasty.

cau_hoi: In 1010, where did King Lý Thái Tổ move the capital from to Đại La?
giai_thich: Hoa Lư was the capital of the Đinh and Early Lê dynasties, with a rugged terrain suitable for defense but cramped and difficult for development. Lý Thái Tổ recognized that the country had stabilized and needed a central capital for economic and cultural development. Legend has it that when the king's boat docked at Đại La, a golden dragon flew up, prompting the king to rename it Thăng Long.

cau_hoi: When was the Lý dynasty established?
giai_thich: At the end of 1009, King Lê Long Đĩnh died. Lý Công Uẩn, then the commander of the palace guard, was supported by the court officials and monk Vạn Hạnh to ascend the throne, establishing the Lý dynasty. The following year, in 1010, he moved the capital to Thăng Long. The Lý dynasty lasted 216 years (1009 – 1225) with 9 kings, being the dynasty that saw the most brilliant development of Buddhism.

cau_hoi: The poem "Nam quốc sơn hà" is often referred to by researchers as what?
A: The first law code of Vietnam
B: The first love poem of Vietnam
C: The first declaration of independence of Vietnam
D: The first national anthem of Vietnam
giai_thich: The poem asserts that the land of Nam belongs to the people of Nam, a fact that has been "determined by heaven's decree", and anyone who invades will be defeated. The poem consists of only 4 lines in Hán script but contains a strong spirit of independence. Nguyễn Trãi's Bình Ngô đại cáo is considered the second declaration, and the Declaration of Independence in 1945 is the third.

cau_hoi: What is the real name of the general Lý Thường Kiệt?
giai_thich: Lý Thường Kiệt was born in 1019, originally named Ngô Tuấn. Due to his many contributions, he was granted the surname Lý (the surname of the king). He served three kings of the Lý dynasty for about 50 years, being both a talented general and a skilled politician. He commanded the victory over the Song army in 1076 – 1077 and fought against Champa. He died in 1105 at the age of about 86.

cau_hoi: Who compiled the first historical book of our country, "Great Viet History" (completed in 1272)?
giai_thich: Le Van Huu passed the highest examination in 1247 and was assigned by King Tran Thanh Tong to compile history. The "Great Viet History" consists of 30 volumes, documenting from the time of Trieu Da to the end of the Ly dynasty. The original book has been lost, but much of its content was inherited by Ngo Si Lien in the "Complete History of Great Viet". Le Van Huu is considered the "father" of Vietnamese historiography.

cau_hoi: Mạc Đĩnh Chi, a talented diplomat during the Tran dynasty, was honored with which title?
giai_thich: Mạc Đĩnh Chi passed the top scholar examination in 1304. He had a short and unattractive appearance, so initially King Tran Anh Tong did not want him to pass, but after reading his poem "Lotus in the Jade Well," he was very impressed. When he went on a diplomatic mission to the Yuan dynasty, he responded intelligently and was praised by the Yuan king, leading the people to call him "Dual Nationality Top Scholar".

cau_hoi: The famous physician Tệ Tĩnh during the Tran dynasty is known for which principle in medicine?
A: Only using medicine imported from the North
C: Only treating the king and nobles
giai_thich: Tệ Tĩnh (real name Nguyễn Bá Tĩnh) was a monk and physician in the 14th century. He researched hundreds of medicinal herbs suitable for the climate and physique of Vietnamese people, wrote the books "Southern Medicinal Efficacy" and "Hong Nghia Giac Tu Y Thu". He is considered the "father of Southern medicine". Many Tệ Tĩnh clinics, which provide free medical care in temples, are named after him.

cau_hoi: The renowned physician Hải Thượng Lãn Ông, author of the extensive medical book in the 18th century, was known by what real name?
giai_thich: Lê Hữu Trác (1724 – 1791) abandoned the path of becoming an official, returned to his mother's hometown in Hà Tĩnh to treat the people, adopting the pen name Hải Thượng Lãn Ông (the lazy old man of Hải Thượng), indicating his disdain for fame and fortune. He wrote the "Hải Thượng Y Tông Tâm Lĩnh" consisting of 28 volumes, 66 books. He emphasized medical ethics, considering the medical profession as a "human profession". He is regarded as the father of traditional Vietnamese medicine.

cau_hoi: Lương Thế Vinh, a famous mathematician during the Early Lê dynasty, is popularly known as "Top Scholar of the South" and is the author of which mathematics book?
giai_thich: Lương Thế Vinh passed the top scholar examination in 1463 during the reign of King Lê Thánh Tông. He was famous for his calculating skills, such as the story of weighing elephants by having them step onto a boat, marking the water level, and then replacing it with stones. The book "Great Mathematical Principles" teaches various calculations and land measurement, used in examinations for many centuries. "Lường" means measurement and calculation.

cau_hoi: The scholar Lê Quý Đôn (18th century) is famous for which encyclopedia?
giai_thich: Lê Quý Đôn (1726 – 1784) passed the second highest examination in 1752 and was known for his intelligence from a young age. "Vân đài loại ngữ" is an encyclopedia documenting the universe, geography, literature, agriculture, and medicine. He also wrote "Phủ biên tạp lục" which recorded the region of Thuận Hóa, Quảng Nam, including notes on the Paracel Islands. He is considered the greatest scholar of the feudal period in Vietnam.

cau_hoi: The female poet Hồ Xuân Hương (late 18th – early 19th century) is known by what title?
giai_thich: Hồ Xuân Hương's Nom poetry is famous for its playful, witty tone and strong personality, daring to criticize injustices against women in feudal society. Her poems "Floating Cake", "Inviting Betel", and "Self-Reflection" are very famous. Poet Xuân Diệu referred to her as "Lady of Nom Poetry". In 2021, UNESCO honored her on the occasion of the 250th anniversary of her birth.

cau_hoi: Who compiled the "Complete History of Great Viet", the most important official history of Vietnam during the feudal period?
giai_thich: In 1479, under King Lê Thánh Tông, historian Ngo Si Lien compiled a history book based on the works of Le Van Huu and Phan Phu Tien, consisting of 15 volumes, documenting from the time of Hồng Bàng to when Lê Lợi ascended the throne. Later historians continued to write. The printed version in 1697 (the Cabinet version) is the oldest complete copy remaining.

cau_hoi: The folk verse "First is Kinh Ky, second is Pho Hien" refers to which bustling trading port in today's province?
giai_thich: Pho Hien thrived in the 17th – 18th centuries, being a hub for merchants from China, Japan, the Netherlands, England, and France. Foreign merchant ships had to stop here to complete procedures before heading to Thang Long (Kinh Ky). Today, Hung Yen still has many relics such as Hien Pagoda, Văn Miếu Xích Đằng, and the assembly halls of the Chinese community. Later, Pho Hien declined due to river siltation.

cau_hoi: Which French archaeologist was the first to discover and name the 'Bắc Sơn Culture' in Lạng Sơn in 1924, paving the way for the study of the Stone Age in Vietnam?
giai_thich: Henri Mansuy was a French geologist and paleontologist from the Indochina Geological Department, who discovered the first cave relics in Bắc Sơn district, Lạng Sơn province. The Bắc Sơn culture is famous for its characteristic polished stone tools and early signs of agriculture. Later, Madeleine Colani continued to collaborate and excavate the Hòa Bình culture, clarifying the origins of prehistoric people in Vietnam.

cau_hoi: When did the first resistance of the Trần dynasty against the Mongol army take place?
giai_thich: In early 1258, about 30,000 Mongol troops along with Đại Lý forces invaded our country. After the Battle of Bình Lệ Nguyên, the court retreated from Thăng Long, implementing a 'vacant garden' strategy. The Mongol army entered Thăng Long but lacked supplies and was counterattacked by the Trần forces at Đông Bộ Đầu, forcing them to retreat. This was a rare defeat for the Mongol army at that time.

cau_hoi: Which king of the Trần dynasty led the resistance against the Mongol army in 1258?
giai_thich: Trần Thái Tông (Trần Cảnh) was the first king of the Trần dynasty. During the resistance, he personally led troops into battle at Bình Lệ Nguyên. He was also knowledgeable in Buddhist studies and wrote works such as 'Khóa hư lục'. After the victory, he abdicated in favor of his son Trần Thánh Tông and became the retired emperor, starting this tradition in the Trần dynasty.

cau_hoi: Who was the Mongol general that commanded the first invasion of Đại Việt in 1258?
giai_thich: Ngột Lương Hợp Thai (Uriyangqadai) was the son of the famous general Tốc Bất Đài, who had participated in campaigns in Europe. He conquered the Đại Lý kingdom (Yunnan) before advancing into Đại Việt. Thoát Hoan, Ô Mã Nhi, and Toa Đô were generals of the Yuan dynasty in the second and third invasions.

cau_hoi: In 1282, which conference did King Trần Nhân Tông convene with lords and officials to discuss strategies against the Yuan invaders?
giai_thich: The Bình Than Conference (in Hải Dương) was held on a boat at Bình Than port, involving lords and generals to assign leadership and prepare forces. By 1284, the court organized the Diên Hồng Conference with elders to gather public opinion. The story of Trần Quốc Toản crushing an orange occurred during the Bình Than Conference.

cau_hoi: The saying 'I would rather be a demon of the South than a king of the North' belongs to which general?
giai_thich: In 1285, Trần Bình Trọng commanded the defense at Thiên Mạc to ensure King Trần's safe retreat. He was captured by the Yuan troops. The enemy general tempted him, asking if he wanted to be a king in the North, to which he boldly replied with the above saying and refused to eat or drink. The Yuan troops executed him. This saying has become a symbol of indomitable spirit.

cau_hoi: The poem 'Tụng giá hoàn kinh sư' (Returning the Emperor to the Capital), with the line 'Seizing the boat at Chương Dương, Holding the river at Hàm Tử', is by whom?
giai_thich: Trần Quang Khải was the Grand Marshal and commander of the Battle of Chương Dương in 1285, defeating the Yuan army and liberating Thăng Long. After the victory, while escorting the two kings back to the capital, he composed a poem praising the victory and reminding that 'Peace should be strived for, that land should last for a thousand years'. He was the son of King Trần Thái Tông.

cau_hoi: In 1287, where did General Trần Khánh Dư destroy the fleet carrying supplies for the Yuan army?
giai_thich: The supply fleet of about 700,000 stone was commanded by Trương Văn Hổ, following the Yuan navy led by Ô Mã Nhi. Trần Khánh Dư ambushed at Vân Đồn (Quảng Ninh) and sank the entire fleet. Without supplies, the Yuan troops in Vạn Kiếp and Thăng Long faced starvation and had to consider retreating. The Battle of Vân Đồn set the stage for the victory at Bạch Đằng in 1288.

cau_hoi: Which Yuan general was beheaded in the Tây Kết battle in 1285?
giai_thich: Toa Đô (Sogetu) led the Yuan troops from Champa to attack the North. In 1285, during the Tây Kết battle (in Hưng Yên), the Trần forces defeated his army, and Toa Đô was beheaded. Trần Hưng Đạo admired Toa Đô's spirit, saying 'Serving the master should be like this', and then took off his robe to cover his body. After this battle, the Yuan army disintegrated.

cau_hoi: Which military book did Trần Hưng Đạo compile to teach his generals?
giai_thich: 'Binh thư yếu lược' is a book summarizing essential military strategies, compiled by Trần Hưng Đạo for his generals to study. In 'Hịch tướng sĩ', he also reminded the generals to study military texts. 'Hổ trướng khu cơ' is a military book attributed to Đào Duy Từ, while 'Quân trung từ mệnh tập' is a collection of documents by Nguyễn Trãi.

cau_hoi: Where is the main temple of Trần Hưng Đạo, where he passed away, located?
giai_thich: Vạn Kiếp – Kiếp Bạc was an important military base during the resistance against the Yuan and was the fief of Trần Hưng Đạo. He died here in 1300. Every year, the Kiếp Bạc festival takes place in the eighth lunar month, attracting many people. There is a saying 'In the eighth month, we honor Father, in the third month, we honor Mother', where 'Father' refers to Đức Thánh Trần.

cau_hoi: What is the real name of Trần Hưng Đạo?
giai_thich: Trần Quốc Tuấn was the son of An Sinh Prince Trần Liễu, the elder brother of King Trần Thái Tông. "Hưng Đạo" is the title he was bestowed. Despite his father's grievances with the king, Trần Quốc Tuấn prioritized national interests over personal grudges, wholeheartedly supporting the king in fighting against invaders. Before his death, he advised the king to "be lenient with the people to establish deep roots and strong foundations."

cau_hoi: After renouncing the throne to practice Buddhism at Yên Tử, what title was King Trần Nhân Tông given?
giai_thich: After leading the people to victory against the Mongol army twice, Trần Nhân Tông abdicated in 1293, and in 1299 he ascended Yên Tử to practice Buddhism, taking the title Trúc Lâm Đầu Đà. He traveled everywhere encouraging people to abandon superstitions and do good deeds. He was honored as the Buddha King and is considered the founder of the Trúc Lâm Zen sect. He passed away in 1308 at Ngọa Vân hermitage.

cau_hoi: The Trần dynasty had a special system where the king would abdicate early to his son but still oversee state affairs together. What was the title given to the abdicated king?
giai_thich: The Grand Emperor system allowed the young king to have a mentor while preventing power struggles within the royal family. During the resistance against the Mongols, Grand Emperor Trần Thánh Tông and King Trần Nhân Tông jointly led the country. The Trần kings often became Grand Emperors while still quite young.

cau_hoi: What special talent did Yết Kiêu, the famous general of Trần Hưng Đạo, possess?
B: Excellent swimmer, able to dive and puncture enemy ships
C: Best elephant rider in the country
giai_thich: Yết Kiêu (real name Phạm Hữu Thế) from Hải Dương was famous for his swimming skills, able to dive underwater for hours. Legend has it that he dived down to use an iron bar to puncture enemy ships. Along with Dã Tượng (skilled in controlling elephants), he was one of the two trusted generals of Trần Hưng Đạo. Many streets are named after him.

cau_hoi: What is the main content of Hồ Quý Ly's "land limitation" policy?
B: Limiting the amount of private land that nobles and landlords could own
giai_thich: At the end of the Trần dynasty, nobles and landlords owned a large amount of land while farmers lacked land.
