In 1397, Hồ Quý Ly enacted the land limitation policy: except for the grand prince and the eldest princess, no one could own more than 10 acres of land; excess land had to be surrendered to the state. He also implemented a servant limitation policy, restricting the number of servants. These reforms weakened the power of the Trần nobility.

cau_hoi: Hồ Nguyên Trừng, son of Hồ Quý Ly, after being captured and taken to the Ming dynasty, was honored as the "ancestor" of which type of weapon?
giai_thich: Hồ Nguyên Trừng invented firearms (a type of cannon) to fight against the Ming army. After the Hồ dynasty's defeat, he was captured and taken to China. Due to his talent in weapon manufacturing, the Ming dynasty appointed him as an official in the Ministry of Public Works. The Ming would often pay homage to him when worshipping firearms, calling him the "ancestor of gunpowder weapons." He also wrote the book "Nam Ông mộng lục" about Vietnamese figures.

cau_hoi: The Hồ dynasty's resistance against the Ming army failed, and our country fell under Ming rule in which year?
giai_thich: At the end of 1406, the Ming dynasty used the pretext of "supporting Trần and destroying Hồ" to invade with about 200,000 troops. Despite the strong fortifications of Đa Bang, the Hồ dynasty lacked popular support and quickly faced defeat. In 1407, Hồ Quý Ly and his son were captured, and the Ming dynasty established its rule, renaming our country as Giao Chỉ. Hồ Nguyên Trừng once said: "I am not afraid of fighting, only afraid that the people's hearts do not follow."

cau_hoi: In 1416, how many loyal followers did Lê Lợi gather to organize the Lũng Nhai Oath, pledging to live and die together to fight against the Ming?
giai_thich: The Lũng Nhai Oath took place in the mountainous region of Lam Sơn (Thanh Hóa), consisting of Lê Lợi and 18 loyal comrades, including Lê Lai. They swore to "live and die together" and collaborated to plan the fight against the invaders to save the country. Two years later, in 1418, the Lam Sơn uprising officially broke out.

cau_hoi: In which province today did the Battle of Xương Giang in 1427, where the Lam Sơn insurgents defeated most of the Ming reinforcements, take place?
giai_thich: After Liễu Thăng was executed at Chi Lăng, his deputy Lương Minh and other generals continued to march towards Xương Giang. The insurgents surrounded and annihilated this entire army, capturing tens of thousands of prisoners. The victories at Chi Lăng and Xương Giang were decisive for the success of the resistance. According to the administrative arrangement in 2025, Bắc Giang province will be merged with Bắc Ninh.

cau_hoi: The Battle of Tốt Động – Chúc Động in 1426, a major victory for the Lam Sơn insurgents, took place in which area?
D: Southwest area of Đông Quan (present-day Hanoi)
giai_thich: In November 1426, Vương Thông led about 100,000 Ming troops to attack the insurgents. The insurgents ambushed at Tốt Động and Chúc Động (Chương Mỹ district, Hanoi), defeating the Ming army and killing tens of thousands. Vương Thông was injured and had to retreat to defend Đông Quan (Thăng Long). After this battle, the insurgents besieged Đông Quan.

cau_hoi: In 1427, which general of the Ming dynasty had to surrender and participate in the Dong Quan Oath Conference, committing to withdraw his troops back to China?
giai_thich: After the defeat of the rescue troops, Vuong Thong was tightly besieged in Dong Quan city and was forced to seek peace. In December 1427, the Dong Quan Oath Conference took place. The Lam Son insurgents provided boats, horses, and food for the Ming troops to return home, demonstrating the humanitarian spirit of 'bringing great righteousness to defeat brutality'. About 100,000 Ming troops withdrew.

cau_hoi: Which general proposed to Le Loi the strategy to move the base to Nghe An, a turning point in the Lam Son uprising?
giai_thich: In 1424, when the insurgents faced many difficulties in the Thanh Hoa mountains, Nguyen Chich suggested moving to Nghe An, a vast area with many people and a strategic location where the Ming were weak. Le Loi accepted the plan. From Nghe An, the insurgents gradually liberated the southern regions and then advanced north. This was a turning point that helped the uprising gain the initiative.

cau_hoi: When he ascended the throne in 1428, what era name did Le Loi adopt?
giai_thich: Le Loi ascended the throne in Dong Kinh (Thang Long) and took the era name Thuan Thien, meaning 'in accordance with heaven's will', restoring the national name Dai Viet. He minted coins named 'Thuan Thien Nguyen Bao'. He was King Le Thai To, reigning for about 5 years. Hong Duc was the era name of Le Thanh Tong, Quang Trung was of Nguyen Hue, and Thai Binh was of Dinh Tien Hoang.

cau_hoi: How many provinces did King Le Thanh Tong divide the country into?
giai_thich: In 1466, Le Thanh Tong reformed the administration, dividing the country into 12 provinces and the Trung Do region (Thang Long); in 1471, after expanding the territory to the south, he established the Quang Nam province, raising the total to 13 provinces. Below the provinces were prefectures, districts, counties, and villages. This administrative system was very tight, helping the state manage effectively down to the village level.

cau_hoi: In 1471, which country did King Le Thanh Tong personally lead an attack against, expanding the territory of Dai Viet to the south?
giai_thich: In 1471, Le Thanh Tong led troops to attack Champa, capturing the capital Do Ban (Vijaya, Binh Dinh) and capturing King Tra Toan. The territory of Dai Viet expanded to Quang Nam, Quang Ngai, and the Quang Nam province was established. After this event, the Champa kingdom quickly weakened, leaving only the southern region.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the first map of our country, depicting mountains, rivers, and roads, completed in 1490?
A: Thien Nam Tu Chi Lo Do
C: Dai Nam Nhat Thong Toan Do
giai_thich: In 1469, Le Thanh Tong ordered the provinces to draw local maps, clearly marking mountains, rivers, roads, and seaports. In 1490, these maps were compiled into the 'Hong Duc Ban Do'. The map not only served administrative management but also affirmed territorial sovereignty. 'Dai Nam Nhat Thong Toan Do' is a map from the Nguyen dynasty.

cau_hoi: In what year did the stone steles recording the names of the doctors at Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam begin to be erected?
giai_thich: In 1484, King Le Thanh Tong ordered the erection of steles inscribing the names of doctors, starting from the examination of 1442, to honor talented individuals and encourage learning. Each stele is placed on the back of a stone turtle, symbolizing longevity. Currently, rubbing the turtle's head has been banned to protect the heritage. The examination of 1442 was overseen by Nguyen Trai.

cau_hoi: Currently, how many steles of doctors are preserved at Van Mieu - Quoc Tu Giam?
giai_thich: There are 82 steles inscribing the names of 1,304 doctors from 82 examinations from 1442 to 1779. These steles are not only historical heritage but also works of art with different decorative patterns through each period. In 2010, the 82 doctor steles were recognized by UNESCO as a World Documentary Heritage (Memory of the World Programme), which also marked the 1,000th anniversary of Thang Long.

cau_hoi: In 1527, who deposed the early Le dynasty and established the Mac dynasty?
giai_thich: Mac Dang Dung was originally a fisherman, passed the martial arts exam and gradually became the most powerful minister at the end of the early Le dynasty. In 1527, he forced King Le Cung Hoang to abdicate and established the Mac dynasty. Later, the former ministers of the Le dynasty reestablished the Le dynasty in Thanh Hoa, leading to a period of Southern and Northern courts lasting about 60 years. Mac Dinh Chi was his ancestor.

cau_hoi: Who was the founder of the Trinh lords in the North?
giai_thich: Nguyen Kim was the one who restored the Le dynasty (Le Trung Hung) to oppose the Mac dynasty. After Nguyen Kim died in 1545, his son-in-law Trinh Kiem took full military power. From then on, the Trinh lords held real power in the North, while King Le was merely a puppet, known as the period of 'Le kings and Trinh lords'. Trinh Tung was the one who overthrew the Mac dynasty in Thang Long in 1592.

cau_hoi: In 1558, who was appointed to govern the Thuan Hoa region, marking the beginning of the Nguyen lords' rule in the South?
giai_thich: Nguyen Hoang was the second son of Nguyen Kim. Fearing for his life after his brother Nguyen Uong was killed by his brother-in-law Trinh Kiem, he requested to govern the wild land of Thuan Hoa. He skillfully built up his forces, reclaimed land, and attracted settlers. The subsequent Nguyen lords expanded their territory southward, laying the foundation for present-day Vietnam.

cau_hoi: During the second resistance against the Yuan-Mongol invasion (1285), which young general of the Tran dynasty bravely fought and heroically sacrificed himself in the battle at Tay Ket ferry?
giai_thich: Tran Quoc Toan, being too young, was not allowed to attend the military conference at Binh Than, which made him so angry that he crushed an orange in his hand without realizing it. Upon returning, he self-recruited thousands of young men and servants, embroidered a large flag with the six golden words 'Defeat the strong enemy, repay the royal grace,' and achieved many glorious victories. He heroically fell at just over 16 years old while pursuing the enemy along the Red River, becoming a shining example of youthful heroism.

cau_hoi: The saying "Hoanh Son nhat doi, van dai dung than" (A stretch of Hoanh Son can sustain generations) is believed to be advice from whom to Nguyen Hoang?
giai_thich: According to legend, when Nguyen Hoang sent someone to ask for advice on how to protect himself, the sage Nguyen Binh Khiem pointed to the mountain range and said the above phrase, suggesting he should move south of the Hoanh Son range (Deo Ngang) to establish a long-term career. Nguyen Hoang followed this advice and requested to govern Thuan Hoa. The story shows that Nguyen Binh Khiem was respected by many factions.

cau_hoi: The Thầy Fort, a system of fortifications that helped the Nguyen lords stop the Trinh army in Quang Binh, was designed by whom?
giai_thich: Dao Duy Tu was a talented individual from the North, but due to his background as a performer, he could not take the exams. He came to the South to assist Lord Nguyen Phuc Nguyen, building the Trường Dục and Nhat Le fortifications that stretched for dozens of kilometers. The locals called it 'Thầy Fort' to honor him. He is also regarded as the founder of the traditional Vietnamese theater art (tuong).

cau_hoi: In the 17th century, how many times did the Trinh and Nguyen lords fight each other?
giai_thich: From 1627 to 1672, the Trinh and Nguyen armies fought 7 times in the Quang Binh and Ha Tinh regions. The wars caused significant losses in lives and property, with neither side emerging victorious. In 1672, both sides made peace, using the Gianh River as the boundary. For nearly 100 years afterward, there were no major conflicts, and the Nguyen lords focused on expanding their territory southward.

cau_hoi: In 1698, who was appointed by Lord Nguyen Phuc Chu to oversee the southern lands and establish Gia Dinh province?
giai_thich: Nguyen Huu Canh (Nguyen Huu Kinh) laid the foundation for the administrative apparatus in the Dong Nai – Gia Dinh region, establishing Gia Dinh province with two districts: Phuoc Long and Tan Binh, and recruiting settlers to reclaim land. In 1998, Ho Chi Minh City celebrated the 300th anniversary of Saigon – Gia Dinh. He is worshipped in many temples and shrines in the South.

cau_hoi: Mac Cuu, originally from Guangdong (China), contributed to the reclamation of which area in the southwest and then offered it to the Nguyen lord?
giai_thich: Mac Cuu refused to submit to the Qing dynasty, so he migrated south, reclaiming the Ha Tien area and establishing a bustling trade center. In 1708, he requested to submit to the Nguyen lord and was appointed as the General of Ha Tien. His son, Mac Thien Tu, continued to develop Ha Tien into a cultural center with the 'Tao Dan Chieu Anh Cac'.

cau_hoi: "The Rebellion of the Proud Soldiers" occurred in the North in the 18th century; what was it?
B: Tam Phu soldiers, relying on their contributions to support the lord, became arrogant and unruly
giai_thich: The Tam Phu soldiers were recruited from three districts in Thanh Hoa and Nghe An, the homeland of the Trinh lord. In 1782, after Lord Trinh Sam died, they participated in overthrowing the crown prince Trinh Can to install Trinh Tong on the throne. From then on, they became arrogant, burning and looting the houses of officials, demanding rewards, and even intervening in the appointment of lords. The folk saying 'Tam Phu soldiers' refers to this chaos.

cau_hoi: In which year did the Tay Son movement erupt?
giai_thich: In 1771, the three brothers Nguyen Nhac, Nguyen Hue, and Nguyen Lu raised the flag of rebellion in Tay Son Thượng đạo (now An Khe, Gia Lai). The slogan 'take from the rich to give to the poor' attracted a large number of peasants, merchants, and even ethnic minorities. In a short time, the insurgents captured Quy Nhon city using a strategy where Nguyen Nhac pretended to be captured and locked in a cage.

cau_hoi: In 1778, what era name did Nguyen Nhac adopt when he ascended to the throne?
giai_thich: Nguyen Nhac was the eldest brother of the Tay Son trio. He ascended to the throne in 1778, establishing his capital at Do Ban (Binh Dinh) and changing his title to Emperor. Later, when Nguyen Hue ascended as Quang Trung (1788), Nguyen Nhac demoted himself to 'Tay Son King'. Canh Thinh was the era name of Nguyen Quang Toan, the son of Quang Trung.

cau_hoi: In 1786, what was the slogan used by Nguyễn Huệ when he first marched north?
giai_thich: Taking advantage of the chaos in the North, Nguyễn Huệ marched north under the pretext of "helping the Lê king, destroying the Trịnh lord." He quickly eliminated the Trịnh regime, ending over 200 years of Lê kings and Trịnh lords. King Lê Hiển Tông married his daughter, Princess Lê Ngọc Hân, to Nguyễn Huệ. He then returned power to the Lê king and withdrew to the South.

cau_hoi: Who was the last king of the Lê dynasty that fled to seek help from the Qing dynasty, leading to the invasion in 1788?
giai_thich: Lê Chiêu Thống was the grandson of King Lê Hiển Tông. When threatened by the Tây Sơn army, he fled to the Qing dynasty for help. Emperor Qianlong took this opportunity to send troops to invade. After the defeat of the Qing army in 1789, Lê Chiêu Thống lived in exile in Beijing, had to shave his head and braid his hair like a Manchu, and died there in 1793. His act of "carrying a snake to bite the chicken at home" was criticized by later generations.

cau_hoi: When attacking the Ngọc Hồi fortress in 1789, what type of shield did the Tây Sơn army use to avoid the Qing army's firepower?
B: Wooden planks covered with wet straw
giai_thich: The Ngọc Hồi fortress was the most fortified base of the Qing army, equipped with cannons and iron spikes. King Quang Trung ordered his troops to assemble wooden planks into large shields, wrapped in wet straw on the outside, with 20 men carrying each shield, followed by those wielding short knives. The Qing army's bullets and rockets could not penetrate. Combined with war elephants, the Tây Sơn army broke the Ngọc Hồi fortress in the early hours of the 5th day of Tet.

cau_hoi: After King Quang Trung died, who succeeded the Tây Sơn dynasty?
giai_thich: Nguyễn Quang Toản was the son of Quang Trung, ascending the throne in 1792 at about 10 years old, adopting the era name Cảnh Thịnh. Due to his young age, court officials fought for power, killing each other, which quickly weakened the Tây Sơn dynasty. In 1802, Nguyễn Ánh defeated the Tây Sơn, and Quang Toản was captured and executed.

cau_hoi: Which French bishop assisted Nguyễn Ánh in the fight against the Tây Sơn and took Prince Cảnh to France?
giai_thich: Bá Đa Lộc met Nguyễn Ánh while he was fleeing from the Tây Sơn army. In 1787, he took Prince Cảnh, then 7 years old, to France to sign the Versailles treaty for aid, but France was in crisis, so the treaty was not implemented. He raised funds, bought weapons, and recruited some French officers to assist Nguyễn Ánh. He died in 1799.

cau_hoi: The Imperial City of Huế was built in an architectural style that combines Eastern elements with the fortification style of which famous military architect?
giai_thich: The Imperial City of Huế is nearly square, each side about 2.5 km, built from 1805. The walls were constructed in the French Vauban fortress style, with protruding bastions at the corners. Inside, it followed Eastern principles with the Royal City, Forbidden City, and a view overlooking the Perfume River and Ngự Bình Mountain. This is the largest military architectural work in Vietnam during the feudal period.

cau_hoi: What is the official code of law of the Nguyễn dynasty, issued during King Gia Long's reign in 1815, called?
C: Hoàng Việt luật lệ (Gia Long Law)
giai_thich: The Hoàng Việt luật lệ consists of 398 articles, primarily compiled based on the laws of the Qing dynasty. Compared to the Hồng Đức Code of the Lê dynasty, the Gia Long law is considered harsher and offers less protection for women's rights. The code was used throughout the Nguyễn dynasty, and the French once translated it into French for study.

cau_hoi: In the administrative reform of 1831 – 1832, what administrative units did King Minh Mạng divide the country into?
giai_thich: Previously, the country was divided into Bắc Thành, Gia Định Thành, and various districts directly under the capital. Minh Mạng abolished the cities and established 30 provinces along with Thừa Thiên prefecture (the capital), each province headed by a Tổng đốc and a Tuần phủ. Many province names and boundaries from Minh Mạng's time have been retained until recently. This was the largest administrative reform of the feudal period.

cau_hoi: According to the "Tứ bất" rule of the Nguyễn dynasty, there are four things that cannot be established. Which of the following is one of them?
giai_thich: "Tứ bất" refers to four prohibitions: no prime minister appointed, no top scholar selected, no empress established, and no titles granted to outsiders of the royal family. The purpose was to concentrate power in the hands of the king and prevent others from encroaching on authority. However, this rule was not strictly enforced; for example, King Bảo Đại appointed Nam Phương as empress in 1934.

cau_hoi: Which agency compiled the major official history "Đại Nam thực lục" of the Nguyễn dynasty?
A: National History Institute of the Nguyễn dynasty
giai_thich: The National History Institute was established in 1821 during Minh Mạng's reign, specializing in compiling historical records. "Đại Nam thực lục" records events according to each Nguyễn lord and king, consisting of hundreds of volumes, and is the most important source of information about the Nguyễn period. The book also documents many details about how the Nguyễn dynasty managed the Paracel and Spratly Islands.

cau_hoi: Poet and military leader Nguyễn Công Trứ was instrumental in reclaiming land and establishing which two coastal districts?
C: Kim Sơn (Ninh Bình) and Tiền Hải (Thái Bình)
giai_thich: In 1828 – 1829, Nguyễn Công Trứ served as the land reclamation envoy, recruiting poor people to build dikes and reclaim land, establishing the two districts of Kim Sơn and Tiền Hải, helping thousands of people gain farmland. The locals built a temple to honor him as the founder of the land. He was also a poet with many famous folk songs, including the line "Having a reputation in the world, one must have a name with the mountains and rivers."

cau_hoi: In 1858, which coalition attacked Da Nang, marking the beginning of the invasion of Vietnam?
giai_thich: Spain participated to protect Spanish missionaries who were being suppressed by the Nguyễn court. Spanish troops were mainly sent from the Philippines. After the Treaty of Nhâm Tuất in 1862, Spain received compensation for war expenses and withdrew, while France occupied the territory. Many Filipino soldiers participated in this conflict.

cau_hoi: In 1861, which stronghold did Nguyễn Tri Phương command the troops and people against the French in Gia Định?
giai_thich: Chí Hòa Stronghold was a major defensive line about 12 km long near Saigon. In February 1861, French forces attacked with heavy firepower. After two days of fierce fighting, the stronghold fell, Nguyễn Tri Phương was wounded, and his younger brother Nguyễn Duy was killed. In 1873, when the French attacked Hanoi, Nguyễn Tri Phương was severely injured and chose to starve to death rather than allow the French to treat him.

cau_hoi: In 1867, which high-ranking official committed suicide by poison after failing to retain the three provinces of Western Nam Kỳ against the French?
giai_thich: Phan Thanh Giản was the first person from Nam Kỳ to pass the doctoral exam and led a delegation to France in 1863 to negotiate the return of the three eastern provinces but was unsuccessful. In 1867, when the French occupied the three western provinces, he felt resistance was futile and surrendered the city to avoid civilian casualties, then starved himself and committed suicide with poison. Hoàng Diệu committed suicide when Hanoi fell in 1882.

cau_hoi: The blind patriotic poet Nguyễn Đình Chiểu is the author of which famous Nôm poem?
giai_thich: Nguyễn Đình Chiểu (1822 – 1888) became blind in both eyes at a young age but still opened a school, practiced medicine, and wrote poetry against the French. "Lục Vân Tiên" tells the story of Vân Tiên, who values righteousness over wealth, and is well-known among the people of the South. He also wrote "Văn tế nghĩa sĩ Cần Giuộc," the best elegy for the farmers who fought against the invaders.

cau_hoi: In 1873, French officer Francis Garnier, who led the first attack on Hanoi, was killed where?
giai_thich: After capturing Hanoi, Garnier led his troops outside the citadel. On December 21, 1873, the Black Flag Army of Lưu Vĩnh Phúc, in coordination with the imperial troops, ambushed him at Cầu Giấy and killed him. This victory caused panic among the French forces. However, the court in Huế signed the Treaty of Giáp Tuất in 1874, ceding six provinces of Nam Kỳ to France.

cau_hoi: In 1883, French officer Henri Rivière was killed in the second battle of Cầu Giấy by which forces?
C: Black Flag Army of Lưu Vĩnh Phúc in coordination with the imperial troops
giai_thich: In 1882, Rivière captured Hanoi for the second time, and Governor Hoàng Diệu committed suicide. On May 19, 1883, the Black Flag Army of Lưu Vĩnh Phúc, along with Hoàng Kế Viêm's troops, ambushed Rivière at Cầu Giấy and killed him. The Black Flag Army was originally a Chinese force that fled to Vietnam and was used by the Huế court to fight against the French in the North.

cau_hoi: The treaty of 1883, signed immediately after France attacked the Thuận An estuary, recognizing French protectorate over Bắc Kỳ and Trung Kỳ, is known as what?
giai_thich: In August 1883, taking advantage of the recent death of Emperor Tự Đức and the turmoil in the court, France attacked the Thuận An estuary, threatening the capital Huế. On August 25, 1883, the court was forced to sign the treaty drafted by Jules Harmand. The Patenôtre Treaty in 1884 later only amended some clauses, officially establishing a long-term French protectorate.

cau_hoi: After the fall of the imperial city of Huế in 1885, what annual ceremony do the people of Huế hold on the 23rd day of the 5th lunar month to commemorate those who died?
D: Ceremony for the souls of the dead
giai_thich: On the night of the 22nd to the 23rd of the 5th lunar month in the year of the Rooster (1885), the war faction attacked the French at the Mang Cá fort and the French consulate but failed. The French counterattacked, causing thousands of soldiers and civilians to die. Since then, the people of Huế have held a ceremony for the souls of the dead on the 23rd of the 5th lunar month, setting up offerings in front of their homes. This custom is still maintained today.

cau_hoi: During his exile in Algeria, what did King Hàm Nghi study and become?
giai_thich: King Hàm Nghi was exiled to Algeria in 1889 at the age of 18 and lived there until his death in 1943. He studied painting with French artists, creating many landscape paintings in the Impressionist style and sculpting. His paintings have been exhibited in Paris and auctioned in recent years. He was the first Vietnamese painter to create oil paintings in the Western style.

cau_hoi: Which Nguyen dynasty king is famous for being the first to cut his hair short, drive a car, and was deposed by the French in 1907 for his anti-French sentiments?
giai_thich: Thanh Thai ascended the throne in 1889 at the age of 10. He had reformist ideas, was interested in Western civilization, and often disguised himself to understand the lives of the people. He covertly opposed the French, leading them to falsely accuse him of being mentally ill and forcing him to abdicate in 1907. He was later exiled to Réunion Island with his son, King Duy Tan.

cau_hoi: In which year did the major tax resistance movement of farmers in Central Vietnam, which spread from Quang Nam, take place?
giai_thich: In early 1908, farmers from Quang Nam marched to the provincial office demanding tax reductions and less forced labor. The movement quickly spread to other provinces in Central Vietnam, with many people cutting their hair short in the spirit of reform, leading the French to call them "the shaved head rebels." The French colonialists brutally suppressed the movement, arresting many intellectuals, including Phan Chau Trinh, who was exiled to Con Dao.

cau_hoi: In 1908, what was the "Hanoi poisoning" plan of the patriots?
A: Burning down the French oil depot
D: Poisoning the food of French soldiers in Hanoi to incite a rebellion
giai_thich: On June 27, 1908, some patriotic cooks poisoned the food of about 200 French artillery soldiers in Hanoi, intending to take advantage of the situation for the insurgents led by De Tham to seize the city. However, the poison was not strong enough, and the French soldiers only suffered from food poisoning, leading to the plan being exposed. The French colonialists executed 13 people. This event highlighted the strong anti-French spirit in urban areas.

cau_hoi: Who founded the patriotic organization "Vietnam Quang Phuc Hội," established in 1912 in Guangzhou (China) with the goal of establishing the Democratic Republic of Vietnam?
giai_thich: Influenced by the Xinhai Revolution in China in 1911, Phan Boi Chau abandoned the constitutional monarchy approach and founded the Vietnam Quang Phuc Hội, aiming to expel the French, restore Vietnam, and establish a republic. The organization carried out several assassination attempts and the 1916 uprising, which King Duy Tan participated in, but all failed.

cau_hoi: The verse "The revenge is not yet paid, but my hair has turned gray, How many times have I sharpened my sword under the moon" in the poem "Cam Hoai" is by whom?
giai_thich: Dang Dung was a general of the Later Tran dynasty, alongside King Trung Quang De fighting against the Ming army after the Ho dynasty's defeat. The poem "Cam Hoai" expresses the pain of a fallen hero who still harbors great ambitions. In 1413, he was captured by the Ming army and jumped into the sea to commit suicide on the way to being taken back north. The poem is considered one of the best works of the medieval period.

cau_hoi: In 1924, where did Pham Hong Thai throw a bomb to assassinate the Governor-General of Indochina Merlin at a hotel?
giai_thich: On June 19, 1924, Pham Hong Thai threw a bomb at a welcome party for Governor Martial Merlin at the Victoria Hotel in the Sa Diện concession (Guangzhou). Merlin escaped unharmed, but the explosion made a significant impact, known as the "Sa Diện bomb." Being pursued, Pham Hong Thai jumped into the Zhujiang River and sacrificed himself at the age of 28. He was buried in Hoang Hoa Cemetery.

cau_hoi: Who is the leader of the Vietnam Nationalist Party, who led the Yen Bai uprising in 1930?
giai_thich: The Vietnam Nationalist Party was established in 1927, modeled after the Chinese Nationalist Party. On the night of February 9, 1930, the uprising broke out in Yen Bai and several other places but quickly failed. Nguyen Thai Hoc and 12 comrades were executed by the French. Before sacrificing themselves, they shouted "Long live Vietnam!" His famous saying is "Success or failure, one becomes a person."

cau_hoi: In 1920, which thesis did Nguyen Ai Quoc read and find the path to save the country and liberate the nation?
A: Lenin's thesis on the national and colonial question
B: Sun Yat-sen's Three Principles of the People
C: The French Declaration of Human Rights
giai_thich: In July 1920, Nguyen Ai Quoc read the "Draft of the First Thesis on the National and Colonial Question" by Lenin published in the Humanitarian newspaper (France). He recounted: "Lenin's thesis moved me deeply, excitedly, and clarified my beliefs!" In December 1920, he participated in founding the French Communist Party.

cau_hoi: In 1919, on behalf of Vietnamese patriots in France, Nguyen Ai Quoc sent the "Demands of the Annamese People" to which conference?
giai_thich: After World War I, the victorious countries met in Versailles. On June 18, 1919, Nguyen Ai Quoc sent a petition consisting of 8 points, demanding freedom, democracy, and equality for the Vietnamese people, such as freedom of the press and the right to assemble. The petition was not accepted, but it made a significant impact. This was the first time Nguyen Ai Quoc's name appeared in public.

cau_hoi: In 1925, in which city did Nguyen Ai Quoc establish the Vietnam Revolutionary Youth Association?
giai_thich: The Vietnam Revolutionary Youth Association opened training classes for patriotic Vietnamese youth and then sent them back to Vietnam to work. Nguyen Ai Quoc's lectures were compiled into the book "Duong Kach Menh" (1927). The association implemented the "proletarianization" movement, sending members into factories and mines for training. The association was the precursor to communist organizations in Vietnam.

cau_hoi: The Vietnam Revolutionary Press Day (June 21) commemorates the founding of which newspaper established by Nguyen Ai Quoc in 1925?
giai_thich: On June 21, 1925, the first issue of the Youth Newspaper was published in Guangzhou, serving as the mouthpiece of the Vietnam Revolutionary Youth Association. The newspaper was printed on wax paper, with only a few hundred copies of each issue secretly sent back to the country. The 'Pariah Newspaper' (Le Paria) was also founded by Nguyen Ai Quoc earlier in Paris (1922) in French.

cau_hoi: Who was the first General Secretary of the Indochinese Communist Party?
giai_thich: In October 1930, at the first Central Committee meeting in Hong Kong, Tran Phu was elected as General Secretary and drafted the 'Political Platform'. In 1931, he was arrested by the French colonialists and brutally tortured. He sacrificed his life at the age of 27, leaving behind the admonition 'Keep the fighting spirit strong'. Nguyen Van Cu was the General Secretary later (1938 – 1940).

cau_hoi: The revolutionary movement 'Soviet Nghệ - Tĩnh', where the people established self-governance in many villages, occurred during which time?
giai_thich: In 1930, the workers' and peasants' movement surged strongly in Nghe An and Ha Tinh. On September 12, 1930, about 8,000 farmers from Hung Nguyen protested and were bombed by French planes, resulting in nearly 200 deaths. In many places, the colonial government collapsed, and farmers established a Soviet-style government. The movement was brutally suppressed in 1931.

cau_hoi: Which young communist soldier said, 'The path of youth can only be the revolutionary path, it cannot be any other path' before being executed?
giai_thich: Ly Tu Trong (real name Le Van Trong) was born in 1914 in Thailand to a patriotic Vietnamese family. In 1931, while protecting a rally in Saigon, he shot and killed a French secret police officer and was arrested. Due to his age, the French had to try him in a special way. He sacrificed his life at the age of 17. The Young Pioneer team has badges and many movements associated with his example.

cau_hoi: The red flag with a yellow star first appeared in which uprising?
giai_thich: On the night of November 22 to 23, 1940, the Nam Ky uprising broke out in many provinces. The red flag with a five-pointed yellow star, believed to be designed by Nguyen Huu Tien, made its first appearance. The uprising was suppressed, with many soldiers sacrificing their lives, including Nguyen Thi Minh Khai. In 1945, the National Congress in Tan Trao decided to choose the red flag with a yellow star as the national flag.

cau_hoi: Which female hero was executed by the French colonialists in Con Dao in 1952 at the age of about 19?
giai_thich: Vo Thi Sau was from Dat Do (Ba Ria – Vung Tau), participating in the revolution from the age of 14, using grenades to eliminate enemies. In 1950, she was arrested and exiled to Con Dao. Before being executed, she sang loudly and refused to be blindfolded. Her grave in Hang Duong cemetery (Con Dao) is a place many people visit. She was posthumously awarded the title of Hero of the People's Armed Forces.

cau_hoi: The Vietnam Propaganda Liberation Army, the predecessor of the Vietnam People's Army, was established on December 22, 1944, with how many soldiers?
giai_thich: The unit was established in the Tran Hung Dao forest (Cao Bang) under the directive of Ho Chi Minh, led by Vo Nguyen Giap, consisting of 34 soldiers with 34 different types of guns. Just two days later, the unit won two battles at Phai Khat and Na Gan. December 22 every year is celebrated as the founding day of the Vietnam People's Army, also known as the National Defense Day.

cau_hoi: The terrible famine in the Year of the Rooster (1945) in Northern Vietnam caused approximately how many deaths?
giai_thich: The famine occurred due to the Japanese fascists and French colonialists hoarding rice, forcing people to uproot rice to plant hemp, along with natural disasters and crop failures. From late 1944 to mid-1945, about 2 million people in the North died of starvation. The Viet Minh launched the movement 'Break the Japanese rice warehouses to solve the famine', helping to gather the masses in preparation for the August Revolution.

cau_hoi: On March 9, 1945, what important event occurred in Indochina?
A: The French surrendered to the Viet Minh
B: The Soviet Union declared war on Japan
C: The Japanese coup overthrew the French
giai_thich: On the night of March 9, 1945, Japanese troops unexpectedly attacked French forces throughout Indochina. In just one night, the French forces nearly disintegrated, and the Japanese monopolized Indochina. Immediately after, the Party issued the directive 'Japanese-French fighting and our actions', launching a mass movement to resist the Japanese and save the country, paving the way for the August Revolution.

cau_hoi: After abdicating in August 1945, what position was former Emperor Bao Dai invited to hold by the Government of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam?
giai_thich: After abdicating, Bao Dai took the citizen name Vinh Thuy and was invited by President Ho Chi Minh to serve as the Supreme Advisor to the provisional government. He was elected as a representative of the first National Assembly. In 1946, he went to China on a business trip and did not return, later cooperating with the French as the National Chief of the 'Vietnamese Nation' from 1949.

cau_hoi: When did the first general election to elect the National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam take place?
giai_thich: On January 6, 1946, all citizens aged 18 and over, regardless of gender, wealth, ethnicity, or religion, were allowed to vote. About 89% of voters participated despite some areas being sabotaged by the enemy. The first National Assembly consisted of 333 delegates. January 6 is celebrated annually as the day of the first general election of the Vietnamese National Assembly.

cau_hoi: In which year did the National Assembly approve the first Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam?
giai_thich: On November 9, 1946, the first National Assembly approved the first Constitution consisting of 7 chapters and 70 articles, stipulating the rights of freedom, democracy, and the obligations of citizens, with gender equality. November 9 is chosen as Vietnam Law Day. Subsequently, Vietnam had constitutions in 1959, 1980, 1992, and 2013.

cau_hoi: What was the purpose of the "People's Literacy Campaign" launched right after the August Revolution in 1945?
giai_thich: In 1945, about 95% of the Vietnamese population was illiterate. On September 8, 1945, President Ho Chi Minh signed a decree to establish the People's Literacy Department, calling for "those who can read to teach those who cannot." Classes were opened everywhere, even at night, in temples, and some places set up "illiteracy gates" requiring people passing through markets to read. In just one year, about 2.5 million people learned to read and write.

cau_hoi: In which year did the Viet Bac Campaign, which defeated a major French attack on the resistance base, take place?
giai_thich: In October 1947, the French mobilized about 12,000 troops to attack Viet Bac in an attempt to destroy the resistance headquarters. Our troops engaged them on the Lo River (the Bong Lau Pass battle, Khoai Lai) and on Route 4. After 75 days and nights, the French had to retreat. The song "Song Lo" by composer Van Cao was born from this campaign.

cau_hoi: In which year did the Border Campaign, the first major offensive of our army that broke the French encirclement, take place?
giai_thich: The campaign took place from September to October 1950 along Route 4 (Cao Bang – Lang Son), opening the Vietnam-China border. The Dong Khe battle was an important opening battle. President Ho Chi Minh directly went to the front to monitor the campaign. The victory helped our troops gain the initiative on the main battlefield in the North.

cau_hoi: Which hero in the 1950 Border Campaign amputated his severely injured arm to continue fighting?
giai_thich: La Van Cau was a demolition squad leader in the Dong Khe battle. When he was hit, his right arm was shattered, and he asked his comrades to cut it off to avoid hindrance, then continued to carry explosives to attack the fort. In 1952, he was honored as a Military Hero in the first batch. Be Van Dan was a hero who used his body as a gun rest.

cau_hoi: In the Dien Bien Phu Campaign, which hero used his body to block a hole in the fort so that his comrades could rush in to destroy the Him Lam stronghold?
giai_thich: On the night of March 13, 1954, during the opening battle of the campaign, Phan Dinh Ghot was injured but still carried explosives to break the fence, then rushed into the hole of the fort that was firing, allowing his comrades to advance. He sacrificed himself at the age of 31. Many schools and streets are named after him. To Vinh Dien was the one who used his body to block the cannon.

cau_hoi: Which hero used his body to block the wheels of a cannon to prevent it from falling into the abyss while pulling the cannon in Dien Bien Phu?
giai_thich: The cannons, weighing tons, were pulled by soldiers through treacherous mountain passes. When the pulling rope broke, the cannon rolled down the slope, To Vinh Dien rushed in to block the wheels with his body, saving the cannon but sacrificing himself. The story of pulling the cannon in and then pulling it out of the battlefield (following the motto "attack firmly, advance firmly") is recorded in the song "Ho Kéo Pháo."

cau_hoi: Which stronghold was targeted in the opening battle of the Dien Bien Phu Campaign on March 13, 1954?
giai_thich: Him Lam was a stronghold located in the northeast of the stronghold group, referred to by the French as "Béatrice." After about 5 hours of fighting, our troops completely destroyed the stronghold. The French commander here was killed. Hill A1 was the site of the fiercest and longest battle of the campaign. Muong Thanh was where De Castries' command bunker was located.

cau_hoi: The 559th Brigade was established on May 19, 1959, to open a strategic transport route to support the South. What is this route commonly called?
B: Ho Chi Minh Trail (Truong Son Road)
giai_thich: The Ho Chi Minh Trail runs through the western mountains and forests, stretching thousands of kilometers with a dense network of branches, including through Laos and Cambodia. Hundreds of thousands of soldiers and youth volunteers worked on this route. The U.S. dropped millions of tons of bombs to cut off the road but failed. There was even a pipeline for oil and gasoline stretching thousands of kilometers.

cau_hoi: In which province did the "Dawn Uprising" movement in 1960 first erupt strongly?
giai_thich: On January 17, 1960, the people of three communes: Định Thủy, Phước Hiệp, and Bình Khánh (Mỏ Cày district, Bến Tre) rose up. The movement spread throughout the South and the Central Highlands. In Bến Tre, there was the "Long-Haired Army," a famous political struggle force led by Mrs. Nguyễn Thị Định. She later became the first female major general of the Vietnam People's Army.

cau_hoi: The famous Cu Chi tunnels, approximately 250 km long, are located in which city?
giai_thich: The tunnels were dug during the resistance against the French and expanded during the American war, featuring multiple levels with living quarters, smokeless kitchens, surgical stations, water wells, and exits to the Saigon River. Civilians and soldiers lived and fought right beneath the enemy's base. Today, the tunnels are a famous tourist attraction. There are also the famous Vinh Moc tunnels in Quang Tri.

cau_hoi: The Tet Offensive and Uprising of 1968, which attacked most cities in the South, occurred in which year?
giai_thich: On the night of January 30 to February 1, 1968 (Tet Mau Than), the liberation army simultaneously attacked many urban areas, including the US embassy in Saigon. Despite suffering heavy losses, the attack shocked the United States and undermined the will to continue the war. Subsequently, President Johnson announced he would not run for re-election, and the US began negotiations in Paris.

cau_hoi: The "Hanoi Air Defense" battle lasted 12 days and nights at the end of 1972, primarily taking place over which city?
giai_thich: From December 18 to 29, 1972, the US used B-52 strategic bombers to attack Hanoi and Haiphong to exert pressure in negotiations. The northern military and civilians shot down many planes, including dozens of B-52s. Khâm Thiên Street was bombed, resulting in many civilian casualties. The failure forced the US to return to the negotiating table and sign the Paris Agreement in January 1973.

cau_hoi: On what date was the Paris Agreement on ending the war and restoring peace in Vietnam signed?
giai_thich: The negotiations in Paris lasted nearly 5 years (1968 – 1973), making it the longest negotiation in the history of Vietnamese diplomacy. According to the agreement, the US was to withdraw all troops from South Vietnam within 60 days. Mrs. Nguyễn Thị Bình, the Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Provisional Revolutionary Government, was the only female representative to sign the agreement. July 21, 1954, is the date of the signing of the Geneva Agreement.

cau_hoi: On the afternoon of April 30, 1975, which tank number crashed through the main gate and entered the Independence Palace?
giai_thich: Tank 843 arrived first and crashed into the side gate but got stuck, then tank 390 crashed through the main gate. Both tanks have been recognized as national treasures and are currently displayed at the Vietnam Military History Museum (Hanoi) and the Armored Forces Museum. The Independence Palace is now called the Reunification Hall.

cau_hoi: In which year did the first session of the National Assembly of unified Vietnam decide to name the country the Socialist Republic of Vietnam?
giai_thich: After the general election across the country on April 25, 1976, on July 2, 1976, the 6th National Assembly decided on the name of the country, the national flag, the national anthem, the national emblem, and chose Hanoi as the capital. The city of Saigon - Gia Định was renamed Ho Chi Minh City. This event marked the completion of national unification in terms of state.

cau_hoi: The comprehensive "Renovation" process of the country was initiated at which Party Congress in 1986?
giai_thich: The Sixth Congress (December 1986) decided to shift from a centrally planned economy with subsidies to a multi-sector economy operating under market mechanisms. During the subsidy period, people had to use ration cards to buy rice, meat, and fabric. Thanks to Renovation, Vietnam transformed from a food-deficient country to one of the world's leading rice exporters.

cau_hoi: In which year did Vietnam officially become a member of the United Nations?
giai_thich: On September 20, 1977, Vietnam became the 149th member of the United Nations. Vietnam has been elected twice as a non-permanent member of the UN Security Council, for the terms 2008 – 2009 and 2020 – 2021. Vietnam has also participated in UN peacekeeping forces since 2014, with field hospitals in South Sudan.

cau_hoi: On what date did Vietnam officially join the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN)?
giai_thich: Vietnam is the 7th member of ASEAN. In 1998, Vietnam hosted the 6th ASEAN Summit in Hanoi. Vietnam held the ASEAN Chair in 2010 and 2020. August 8, 1967, is the founding date of ASEAN in Bangkok, while January 11, 2007, is the date Vietnam joined the WTO.

cau_hoi: In 2007, Vietnam became the how many member of the World Trade Organization (WTO)?
giai_thich: After about 11 years of negotiations, on January 11, 2007, Vietnam officially became the 150th member of the WTO. Joining the organization facilitated the export of Vietnamese goods to the world and attracted significant foreign investment. Vietnam also participated in many other free trade agreements such as CPTPP and EVFTA (with the European Union).

cau_hoi: Vietnam and the United States officially normalized diplomatic relations in which year?
giai_thich: On July 11, 1995, U.S. President Bill Clinton announced the normalization of relations with Vietnam, following the lifting of the economic embargo in 1994. In 2000, Clinton became the first sitting U.S. president to visit Vietnam after the war. In 2023, the two countries upgraded their relationship to a comprehensive strategic partnership. In the same month of July 1995, Vietnam joined ASEAN.

cau_hoi: Hanoi hosted the first APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in which year?
giai_thich: In November 2006, leaders of 21 APEC member economies met in Hanoi. The leaders wore traditional Vietnamese ao dai during the group photo, a tradition of APEC to wear the host country's attire. In 2017, Vietnam hosted APEC for the second time in Da Nang.

cau_hoi: The central area of the Thang Long Imperial Citadel in Hanoi was recognized by UNESCO as a World Cultural Heritage in which year?
giai_thich: In 2010, coinciding with the 1,000th anniversary of Thang Long – Hanoi, the site was recognized. The archaeological site at 18 Hoang Dieu shows architectural remnants spanning over 1,300 years, from the Dai La, Ly, Tran, Le to Nguyen dynasties. It also includes Doan Mon, Ky Dai (Hanoi Flag Tower), and Hau Lau. UNESCO assessed this as a rare continuous center of power.

cau_hoi: Vietnam's first World Cultural Heritage recognized by UNESCO in 1993 is what?
giai_thich: In 1993, the Complex of Hue Monuments was recognized, including the Citadel, Imperial City, Forbidden City, the tombs of Nguyen kings, Thien Mu Pagoda, and Nam Giao Altar. In 1994, Ha Long Bay became Vietnam's first natural world heritage. In 1999, Hoi An and My Son were recognized. Hue is also the only city in Vietnam with both tangible and intangible cultural heritage recognized by UNESCO.

cau_hoi: Hue Court Music was recognized by UNESCO as a Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage of Humanity in which year?
giai_thich: Hue Court Music is a solemn music used in the rituals of the Nguyen dynasty court, such as the Nam Giao ceremony, coronation ceremony, and longevity celebration. In 2003, it became the first intangible cultural heritage of Vietnam recognized by UNESCO. This was followed by the Central Highlands Gong Culture (2005), Quan Ho, Ca Tru (2009), and many other heritages.

cau_hoi: The art of Ca Tru was included by UNESCO in the list of Intangible Cultural Heritage in Need of Urgent Safeguarding in which year?
giai_thich: Ca Tru (also known as Hat A Dao, Hat Co Dau) is a form of chamber music that combines poetry, featuring a female singer and a musician playing the đàn đáy and a drummer. Ca Tru has a history of hundreds of years, associated with poets like Nguyen Cong Tru and Cao Ba Quat. In 2009, UNESCO listed Ca Tru as needing urgent protection due to the dwindling number of artisans.

cau_hoi: The first documentary heritage of Vietnam recognized by UNESCO in the Memory of the World Program in 2009 is what?
giai_thich: The Nguyen Dynasty woodblocks consist of about 34,000 wooden blocks carved with Chinese and Nom characters, used to print official books of the court such as historical records, laws, and literature. The woodblocks are currently preserved at the National Archives Center IV in Da Lat. In 2010, the 82 doctoral steles at Van Mieu were further recognized, and in 2017, the Nguyen Dynasty Châu bản (regional level) was recognized.

cau_hoi: Who is the youngest laureate in the history of Vietnam's imperial examinations, passing at just 13 years old?
giai_thich: Nguyen Hien (from Nam Dinh) passed the laureate examination in 1247 during the reign of King Tran Thai Tong. He came from a poor family and was intelligent from a young age; the story "Mr. Laureate Flying a Kite" tells how he learned by peeking outside the classroom and used banana leaves as paper. Because he was still young, the king allowed him to return home to learn more etiquette before appointing him as an official. He later rose to the position of Minister of Public Works.

cau_hoi: According to tradition, who is considered the only woman to pass the doctoral examination in feudal Vietnam, who had to disguise herself as a man to take the exam?
giai_thich: Nguyen Thi Due (from Hai Duong) lived during the Mac dynasty, around the 16th – 17th centuries. At that time, women were not allowed to take exams, so she disguised herself as a man to take the exam and achieved high marks. When discovered, King Mac did not punish her but valued her, allowing her to teach in the palace. Later, she also worked for the Le dynasty. Her story still has some details that researchers debate.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the wrongful conviction that led to the execution of Nguyễn Trãi and his family in 1442?
giai_thich: In 1442, King Lê Thái Tông reviewed the troops and stopped to rest at Le Chi Vien (the mulberry garden, Bắc Ninh) of Nguyễn Trãi, then suddenly passed away. The court blamed Nguyễn Thị Lộ, Nguyễn Trãi's concubine, and executed all three of his families. In 1464, King Lê Thánh Tông exonerated Nguyễn Trãi, praising him as 'Ức Trai's heart shines like the Khuê star.'

cau_hoi: The famous Nôm translation of the work 'Chinh phụ ngâm' is often attributed to which female poet?
giai_thich: 'Chinh phụ ngâm' expresses the longing for a husband and the suffering of a wife whose husband is a soldier, reflecting the desire for peace. The translation into the poetic form of song thất lục bát in Nôm is often attributed to Đoàn Thị Điểm, although some researchers suggest it may be by Phan Huy Ích. Đoàn Thị Điểm also wrote the collection 'Truyền kỳ tân phả.'

cau_hoi: Who is the author of the original Chinese text of 'Chinh phụ ngâm'?
giai_thich: Đặng Trần Côn lived in the 18th century and composed 'Chinh phụ ngâm khúc' in Chinese around 1741, during a time of turmoil when many young men had to go to war. The work consists of 476 verses of alternating lines. The Nôm translation is so well-regarded that it has been more widely circulated than the original text. This is an example of a translation becoming a literary masterpiece.

cau_hoi: The work 'Cung oán ngâm khúc', which speaks of the sorrow of a palace maid abandoned by the king, is by whom?
giai_thich: Nguyễn Gia Thiều (1741 – 1798) was the grandson of the Trịnh lord, born into nobility, and once served as a military official. The work consists of 356 verses in the Nôm poetic form, famous for its philosophical verses about life. Along with 'Truyện Kiều' and 'Chinh phụ ngâm', it is considered one of the masterpieces of medieval Nôm literature.

cau_hoi: The poem 'Qua Đèo Ngang' with the line 'Stepping to Đèo Ngang at dusk' is by which female poet?
giai_thich: Bà Huyện Thanh Quan (real name Nguyễn Thị Hinh) lived in the early 19th century and was invited by King Minh Mạng to the palace to teach the palace maids. Her poetry is elegant, melancholic, and nostalgic, such as 'Qua Đèo Ngang' and 'Thăng Long thành hoài cổ'. Đèo Ngang is a natural boundary between Hà Tĩnh and Quảng Bình.

cau_hoi: In 1854, poet Cao Bá Quát led which peasant uprising against the Nguyễn dynasty?
giai_thich: Cao Bá Quát is famous for his talent, with the saying 'The world has four bushels of words, Cao Bá Quát occupies two bushels alone.' Discontent with the court, in 1854, while serving as a teacher in Quốc Oai, he led an uprising with farmers in Mỹ Lương (Hà Nội), called 'Grasshopper Rebels' due to a locust plague that year. He sacrificed himself, and his family was executed. He is referred to as 'Saint Quát.'

cau_hoi: Nguyễn Trường Tộ, who sent many petitions proposing reforms towards the West, lived during the reign of which king?
giai_thich: Nguyễn Trường Tộ (1830 – 1871) was a Catholic from Nghệ An who had traveled to France and Italy. He sent about 30 petitions proposing to open trade, send people to study foreign technology, reform education, and exploit mines. Most of his proposals were not implemented by King Tự Đức and the court. Many believe that if they had been carried out, the country might have been different.

cau_hoi: King Tự Đức was the longest-reigning king of the Nguyễn dynasty. How many years did he rule?
giai_thich: Tự Đức ruled from 1847 to 1883, during the period when French colonialists began to invade Vietnam. He was literate and composed many poems and literary works, but during his reign, the country gradually fell into French hands. He had no biological children due to smallpox as a child, so he had to adopt. After his death, the court fell into crisis with many kings ascending and then being deposed in succession.

cau_hoi: The tomb of King Tự Đức, considered one of the most beautiful tombs in Huế, is officially named what?
giai_thich: Khiêm Lăng was built between 1864 and 1867 while the king was still alive, including a palace area for the king to rest, compose poetry, and fish. The construction of the tomb required a lot of labor, causing soldiers and laborers to revolt in the 'Grasshopper Rebellion' in 1866. Hiếu Lăng is the tomb of Minh Mạng, Gia Lăng (Thiên Thọ Lăng) is the tomb of Gia Long, while Ứng Lăng is the tomb of Khải Định.

cau_hoi: In 1836, King Minh Mạng sent naval forces to which archipelago to mark sovereignty, erect monuments, and survey maps?
giai_thich: In 1836, King Minh Mạng ordered the naval team led by Phạm Hữu Nhật to bring ships to Hoàng Sa, carrying 10 wooden markers to be placed on the islands, clearly stating the year and the name of the person who erected them. These events were recorded in the Nguyễn dynasty's official documents and 'Đại Nam thực lục'. This is an important historical evidence of Vietnam's sovereignty over the Hoàng Sa archipelago.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the main gate, the southern entrance of the Imperial City of Hue?
giai_thich: Ngo Mon was built in 1833 during the reign of Minh Mang, featuring 5 entrances, with the middle one reserved for the king. Above it is the Five Phoenix Pavilion with 9 roofs. Ngo Mon was the site for military parades and the ceremony for announcing doctoral candidates. On August 30, 1945, King Bao Dai abdicated here. Doan Mon is the gate of the Thang Long Citadel in Hanoi.

cau_hoi: What ceremony did the Nguyen kings hold at the Nam Giao altar in Hue?
giai_thich: The Nam Giao altar was built in 1806 in the southern part of the imperial city, consisting of three tiers: the upper circular tier symbolizes heaven, while the middle and lower square tiers symbolize earth. The Nam Giao ceremony is the most important national ritual, where the king prays for favorable weather and peace for the country. This is the only remaining Nam Giao altar in Vietnam. Today, the ceremony is reenacted during the Hue Festival.

cau_hoi: Queen Nam Phuong, the wife of King Bao Dai, was the first to be crowned queen immediately upon marriage during the Nguyen dynasty. What religion did she follow?
giai_thich: Nam Phuong (Nguyen Huu Thi Lan) came from a wealthy family in Go Cong, practiced Catholicism, and studied in France. In 1934, she married King Bao Dai and was crowned queen on the same day, breaking the Nguyen dynasty's 'Four No's' tradition. She participated in many charitable activities, and during the 'Golden Week' in 1945, she donated many pieces of jewelry. She passed away in 1963 in France.

cau_hoi: "Safe Zone" (ATK) Dinh Hoa, where the Central Party and Government worked during the resistance against the French, is located in which province?
giai_thich: ATK Dinh Hoa is located in the mountainous region of northwestern Thai Nguyen province, known as the 'Resistance Capital'. Here is the Khau Ty hut, where President Ho Chi Minh stayed and worked, and Tinh Keo hill, where the Politburo decided to launch the Dien Bien Phu Campaign at the end of 1953. The phrase 'The body is in prison' is another poem by him during his time in captivity in China.

cau_hoi: What is the name of the French military plan in 1953, hoping to achieve a decisive victory in 18 months?
giai_thich: General Navarre was appointed as the commander of French forces in Indochina in 1953, with significant support from the United States. He fortified Dien Bien Phu into 'the strongest stronghold in Indochina', considered by the French and Americans as an 'impregnable fortress'. The defeat at Dien Bien Phu completely ruined Navarre's plan. In 1956, he wrote the book 'Indochina in Death Throes'.

cau_hoi: The Preliminary Agreement on March 6, 1946, between the Democratic Republic of Vietnam and France was signed by President Ho Chi Minh and which French representative?
giai_thich: According to the Preliminary Agreement, France recognized Vietnam as a free nation with its own government, parliament, and military, within the French Union; Vietnam agreed to allow 15,000 French troops to move north to replace Chiang Kai-shek's troops. This was a strategy of 'peace to advance', avoiding simultaneous confrontation with multiple enemies. Sainteny represented the French government in the North.

cau_hoi: What was the purpose of the 'Golden Week' movement in 1945?
A: To hold a gold selling fair
C: To collect gold and money to support the fledgling revolutionary government
giai_thich: After the August Revolution, the national treasury was nearly empty. In September 1945, the government launched the 'Golden Week', calling on the people to voluntarily contribute gold, silver, and money to buy weapons and fund the state. The people across the country supported approximately 370 kg of gold and tens of millions of dong. At the same time, the 'Rice Jar to Save the Hungry' movement helped combat famine.

cau_hoi: In what year was the ancient town of Hoi An recognized by UNESCO as a World Cultural Heritage?
giai_thich: Hoi An was recognized for being a Southeast Asian trading port that has been preserved almost intact, with over 1,000 architectural relics such as ancient houses, assembly halls, temples, ancient wells, and the Japanese Covered Bridge. The architecture blends Vietnamese, Chinese, Japanese, and Western styles. In the same year of 1999, the My Son Sanctuary was also recognized. Hoi An is famous for its lantern-lit nights.

cau_hoi: Which culture in the Red River basin is considered the precursor to the Bronze Age culture, the predecessor of the Dong Son culture?
giai_thich: Phung Nguyen Culture (circa 2000 – 1500 BC) is named after the Phung Nguyen archaeological site in Phu Tho, discovered in 1959. The inhabitants knew how to smelt bronze, create beautifully patterned ceramics, and craft exquisite stone jewelry. This was followed by the Dong Dau and Go Mun cultures, leading to Dong Son. Researchers consider this the period of the formation of the Van Lang state.

cau_hoi: Where were the Vietnamese Khê boat graves, with coffins made from hollowed tree trunks shaped like boats containing many bronze items, found?
giai_thich: In 1961, in Viet Khe commune (Thuy Nguyen, Hai Phong), 5 boat graves belonging to the Dong Son culture, approximately 2,500 years old, were discovered. One large grave contained over 100 bronze artifacts such as drums, jars, spears, and axes. This boat grave is a national treasure. The boat-shaped graves indicate that the Dong Son inhabitants were closely connected to rivers and water.

cau_hoi: Thuc Phan, the founder of the Au Lac state, was the leader of which tribe?
giai_thich: Thuc Phan was the leader of the Au Viet in the northern mountainous region. Around 208 BC, after defeating the Qin army with the Lac Viet, he replaced King Hung, uniting the two tribes Au Viet and Lac Viet into the Au Lac state, taking the title of An Duong Vuong. Some other legends suggest he was a descendant of the king of the Shu state, but researchers still debate this.

cau_hoi: How many walls does the Co Loa Citadel of An Duong Vuong have?
giai_thich: The Co Loa Citadel consists of 3 walls: the Outer Citadel is about 8 km long, the Middle Citadel is about 6.5 km, and the Inner Citadel is rectangular, about 1.6 km. Each wall is surrounded by a water moat connected to the Hoang River, facilitating boat traffic. Folklore states that the citadel has "nine spiral walls," but in reality, archaeologists have confirmed there are 3 walls. This is the largest ancient earthen military construction in Southeast Asia.

cau_hoi: In 1959, archaeologists discovered a cache of bronze arrowheads in the Co Loa area. How many arrowheads were in this cache?
giai_thich: The cache of bronze arrowheads was discovered in Cau Vuc, near the Co Loa citadel, containing tens of thousands of arrowheads, indicating that the Au Lac people had mass bronze casting techniques and powerful weapons. This discovery helps explain the legend of the "divine crossbow" that shoots multiple arrows at once. Archaeologists also found arrowhead molds in Co Loa.

cau_hoi: Si Nhiep, the governor of Giao Chi at the end of the Eastern Han period, encouraged the study of Chinese characters and Confucianism. What title was he later honored with?
giai_thich: Si Nhiep governed Giao Chi for about 40 years (187 – 226) during a time of turmoil in China at the end of the Eastern Han. The Giao Chi region under his rule was relatively stable, attracting many Northern scholars seeking refuge. He was honored by some feudal historians as the "Nam Giao Learning Ancestor" (the ancestor of knowledge in the South), although modern historians have various assessments of his role.

cau_hoi: When he ascended to the throne in 544, what era name did Ly Nam De choose?
giai_thich: Ly Nam De chose the era name Thien Duc (Heaven's Virtue), signifying that the state of Van Xuan was an independent nation on par with the North. He established a court with civil and military officials: Tinh Thieu leading the civil department, Pham Tu leading the military department, and Trieu Quang Phuc as the Left General. Some opinions suggest he also minted coins named "Thien Duc thong bao," but this has not been definitively confirmed.

cau_hoi: During the Northern domination, what area was commonly referred to as "Giao Chi"?
giai_thich: In 111 BC, the Han dynasty conquered Nam Viet and divided the southern territory into several districts, among which the Giao Chi district corresponds to the Northern Delta, the Cuu Chan district is in Thanh Hoa, and the Nhat Nam district covers the area from Nghe An to the south. Later, Northern dynasties and Westerners sometimes used the name Giao Chi to refer to our entire country.

cau_hoi: In 679, what did the Tang dynasty rename Giao Chau?
giai_thich: The Tang dynasty established the An Nam Protectorate with its headquarters in Tong Binh (present-day Hanoi). From then on, the name "An Nam" (meaning "the peaceful south") was used by Chinese dynasties to refer to our country for many centuries, and the French used it to refer to Central Vietnam. In 866, the Tang dynasty changed the An Nam Protectorate to Tinh Hai army.

cau_hoi: Which Tang dynasty official ordered the construction of Dai La citadel (the predecessor of Thang Long capital) in the 9th century?
giai_thich: In 866, Cao Bien expelled the Nan Zhao army and built the Dai La citadel on a large scale, surrounding the central area of present-day Hanoi. Folklore has many legends about Cao Bien, such as him going to suppress the dragon veins of the southern land. In 1010, King Ly Thai To moved the capital to Dai La and renamed it Thang Long.

cau_hoi: Who was the father of Dinh Bo Linh?
C: Dinh Cong Tru, governor of Hoan Chau
giai_thich: Dinh Bo Linh's father was Dinh Cong Tru, who served as the governor of Hoan Chau (Nghe An) under Duong Dinh Nghe and Ngo Quyen. His father died early, and Dinh Bo Linh followed his mother back to their hometown in Hoa Lu. Legends say he was once chased by his uncle, and when he ran across a bridge that broke and fell into the river, a golden dragon appeared to save him, causing his uncle to fear and submit.

cau_hoi: To deter criminals, which king ordered to place a large cauldron of oil in the court and kept tigers in cages, commanding that "anyone who commits a crime will be thrown into the cauldron of oil or fed to the tigers"?
giai_thich: After suppressing the 12 warlords, the country still had many opposing elements. Dinh Tien Hoang used very harsh punishments to maintain order and deter those who intended to rebel. Later historians assessed this as a severe measure, but appropriate for a country just emerging from turmoil. In 979, he was assassinated by an official named Do Thich.

cau_hoi: Which king of the Early Le dynasty is recorded in history as "Ngọa Triều" (the king who lay during court sessions) due to suffering from hemorrhoids and having to lie down while receiving his ministers?
giai_thich: Le Long Dinh ascended the throne in 1005 after killing his brother Le Trung Tong. Historical records describe him as notoriously brutal, indulging in debauchery, and due to his illness, he had to lie down during court sessions. However, some modern researchers suggest that the history written during the Ly dynasty may have exaggerated to justify the Ly dynasty's replacement of the Early Le dynasty. He died in 1009, paving the way for Ly Cong Uan to ascend the throne.

cau_hoi: Which Zen master played an important role in supporting and elevating Ly Cong Uan to the throne in 1009?
giai_thich: Zen Master Van Hanh was Ly Cong Uan's teacher from a young age at Co Phap Pagoda (Bac Ninh). He had great prestige in the court and among the people, believed to possess prophetic abilities. He advocated for Ly Cong Uan's ascension when the Early Le dynasty was in decline. Buddhism flourished during the Ly dynasty, with many monks participating in governance.

cau_hoi: In 1069, after being captured by King Ly Thanh Tong, which Champa king offered the three provinces of Dia Ly, Ma Linh, and Bo Chinh to redeem his life?
giai_thich: In 1069, Ly Thanh Tong and Ly Thuong Kiet led troops against Champa and captured King Che Cu. To be released, Che Cu offered the three provinces (now Quang Binh and northern Quang Tri). The Ly dynasty renamed Dia Ly to Lam Binh and Ma Linh to Minh Linh. This was the first time the territory of Dai Viet expanded southward beyond the Hoanh Son mountain range.

cau_hoi: Which famous upright minister of the Ly dynasty, when nearing death, recommended the talented Tran Trung Ta instead of the devoted caretaker Vu Tan Duong?
giai_thich: When To Hien Thanh fell seriously ill, the deputy minister Vu Tan Duong served him day and night. The empress dowager asked who could replace him, and To Hien Thanh replied with Tran Trung Ta. She was surprised because Vu Tan Duong was devoted, but he explained that if asking about a caretaker, it would be Tan Duong, while for serving the country, it must be Trung Ta. This story became a model of impartiality.

cau_hoi: What is the Chinese title of the work commonly known as "Hich Tuong Si" by Tran Hung Dao?
B: Du Chu Ti Tuong Hich Van
giai_thich: "Du Chu Ti Tuong Hich Van" means "The Hich urging the tì tướng (the generals under command)". The hich was written around 1284, before the second resistance against the Yuan. "Thien Do Chieu" is the Chinese title of "Chieu Doi Do" by Ly Thai To. These works are often studied in the literature curriculum.

cau_hoi: During the resistance against the Yuan, soldiers of the Tran dynasty tattooed the words "Sat That" on their arms. Who does the word "That" refer to here?
giai_thich: "Sat That" means "kill the That Dat invaders", a name used by the Vietnamese and Chinese to refer to the nomadic peoples of the North, including the Mongols. The act of tattooing the words on their arms expressed the determination to fight to the end of the Tran dynasty's soldiers and people. This is a familiar image in literary works and films about the Tran era.

cau_hoi: Which Tran prince was famous for being proficient in the languages and customs of many ethnic groups and commanded the battle of Ham Tu in 1285?
giai_thich: Prince Trần Nhất Duyệt, known as Chiêu Văn Vương, was the son of King Trần Thái Tông, skilled in foreign languages, and understood the customs of many ethnic groups, using his diplomatic talents to attract mountain chieftains. In the battle of Ham Tu (Hung Yen) in 1285, his army included those from the Song dynasty who fled to fight against the Yuan. He was known for his kindness and longevity.

cau_hoi: In 1390, Champa king Che Bong Nga, who had attacked Thang Long multiple times, was shot dead in a naval battle led by which Tran general?
giai_thich: Che Bong Nga was a talented king who made Champa powerful, attacking Thang Long three times in the 1370s and 1380s. In 1390, General Tran Khat Chan ambushed Che Bong Nga's fleet on the Luoc River (Hung Yen). Thanks to a treacherous servant pointing out the king's boat, the Tran troops concentrated their fire and killed Che Bong Nga.

cau_hoi: According to legend, when his father Nguyen Phi Khanh was taken by the Minh army to the North, Nguyen Trai cried as he saw his father off to which border pass and was advised by his father to return and seek revenge for the family and repay the debt to the country?
giai_thich: In 1407, Nguyen Phi Khanh, a high-ranking official of the Ho dynasty, was captured by the Minh army. Nguyen Trai followed his father to Ai Nam Quan (Lang Son). It is said that the father advised: "You should return to seek revenge for the family and repay the debt to the country, rather than following me to cry." Nguyen Trai returned and later participated in the Lam Son uprising. The story is recounted in the poem "Nuoc non nghin dam".

cau_hoi: Nguyen Trai wrote the work "Du Dia Chi". What field does this work cover?
giai_thich: "Du Dia Chi" (1435) is the oldest surviving geographical book of Vietnam, describing the mountains, rivers, products, and customs of various regions of Dai Viet. Nguyen Trai was a versatile figure: a military strategist, politician, writer, poet, and geographer. In 1980, UNESCO recognized him as a World Cultural Celebrity in celebration of the 600th anniversary of his birth.

cau_hoi: Which scholar was responsible for diplomatic relations with the Qing dynasty during King Quang Trung's reign, after the victory in 1789?
giai_thich: Ngô Thì Nhậm (1746 – 1803) was a notable scholar of the Lê dynasty, who supported the Tây Sơn and was trusted by King Quang Trung. After the victory, he drafted skillful diplomatic letters to negotiate peace with the Qing dynasty, maintaining friendly relations and avoiding further conflict. He was also a Zen master, contributing to the revival of the Trúc Lâm Zen sect with his work "Trúc Lâm tông chỉ nguyên thanh."

cau_hoi: The historical novel "Hoàng Lê nhất thống chí", which recounts the late Lê dynasty and the victory of King Quang Trung, is attributed to whom?
giai_thich: "Ngô gia văn phái" is a group of writers from the Ngô Thì family in Tả Thanh Oai village (Hanoi), including Ngô Thì Chí and Ngô Thì Du. The work consists of 17 chapters, written in classical Chinese in a serialized style, recounting historical events quite authentically. Chapter 14 describes the great defeat of the Qing army by King Quang Trung and is included in textbooks.

cau_hoi: After retiring from government, where did scholar Trạng Trình Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm open a school with many famous students?
giai_thich: In 1542, after 8 years serving the Mạc dynasty, Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm submitted a petition to execute 18 corrupt officials, which was not accepted, so he retired to his hometown in Vĩnh Bảo (Hải Phòng) and built Am Bạch Vân to teach. He took the pen name Bạch Vân cư sĩ. His students included many famous figures such as Phùng Khắc Khoan and Lương Hữu Khánh. A temple dedicated to him is located in Vĩnh Bảo.

cau_hoi: Phùng Khắc Khoan (Trạng Bùng), a notable figure during the Lê Trung Hưng period, is credited by folk tradition for bringing which crop variety from China to Vietnam?
giai_thich: When he was sent as an envoy to the Ming dynasty in 1597, Phùng Khắc Khoan is said to have brought back corn (maize) to plant in his homeland and disseminated it among the people. Corn is a crop native to the Americas, introduced to Asia by the Spanish and Portuguese. He also wrote a book "Nông thư" on agricultural techniques. He is worshipped in many places as the "patron of corn cultivation."

cau_hoi: In addition to the Hoàng Sa team, which other team did the Nguyễn lords establish to manage the exploitation of resources and oversee the southern sea and islands, including the Spratly Islands?
giai_thich: According to Lê Quý Đôn's book "Phủ biên tạp lục", in addition to the Hoàng Sa team, there was also the Bắc Hải team, which selected people from Tứ Chính village (Bình Thuận) or Cảnh Dương village to go to the southern islands to collect marine products. The Bắc Hải team was managed by the Hoàng Sa team. This is historical evidence of the Nguyễn lords exercising sovereignty in the East Sea.

cau_hoi: In 1777, when the Tây Sơn army led by Nguyễn Huệ attacked Gia Định and nearly wiped out the Nguyễn lord family, who was the one that managed to escape?
giai_thich: In 1777, the Tây Sơn army captured Gia Định, and lord Nguyễn Phúc Thuần and many members of the royal family were killed. Nguyễn Ánh, then 15 years old and the lord's nephew, escaped to an island and the Hà Tiên region. He faced many failures and had to flee to Siam, but persevered in building his forces for 25 years, ultimately defeating the Tây Sơn and ascending the throne in 1802.

cau_hoi: King Quang Trung planned to move the capital and construct "Phượng Hoàng Trung Đô" in which region?
giai_thich: King Quang Trung believed that Nghệ An was centrally located in the country, convenient for controlling both the North and South, so he ordered the construction of Phượng Hoàng Trung Đô at the foot of Dũng Quyết mountain (now Vinh city) and entrusted La Sơn Phu Tử Nguyễn Thiếp with overseeing the land. The project was still under construction when the king died in 1792, so the plan to move the capital was not realized.

cau_hoi: Who is the author of "Gia Định thành thông chí", an important geographical work about the southern region in the early 19th century?
giai_thich: Trịnh Hoài Đức (1765 – 1825) was a notable figure during the Gia Long – Minh Mạng period, who served as the chief governor of Gia Định. He was one of the "Gia Định tam gia", three famous poets from Gia Định along with Lê Quang Định and Ngô Nhân Tịnh. "Gia Định thành thông chí" meticulously records the geography, climate, customs, products, and history of the southern region.

cau_hoi: The elegy "Ai tư vãn", mourning King Quang Trung, is the work of whom?
giai_thich: Lê Ngọc Hân was the daughter of King Lê Hiển Tông, married to Nguyễn Huệ in 1786, and became the Empress of the Northern Palace. When King Quang Trung suddenly passed away in 1792, she wrote "Ai tư vãn" in Nôm script, in the form of song thất lục bát, expressing her sorrow and praising her husband's merits. She died in 1799 at the age of 29.

cau_hoi: Phan Huy Chú (1782 – 1840) is the author of which famous encyclopedic work about the regimes and regulations through the dynasties?
A: Lịch triều hiến chương loại chí
C: Đại Việt sử ký toàn thư
giai_thich: Phan Huy Chú spent 10 years compiling a book consisting of 49 volumes, divided into 10 categories (fields): geography, figures, officials, rituals, examinations, national resources (finance), criminal law, military organization, literature, and diplomacy. In 1821, he presented the book to King Minh Mạng. This is considered the first encyclopedia of Vietnam.
